item.title: ComfyUI expands to 779 nodes for image, video, and 3D workflows
item.description:
ComfyUI expands to 779 nodes for image, video, and 3D workflows

ComfyUI has grown to include 779 nodes, expanding its capabilities to handle image, video, 3D, and language models along with the plumbing between them. The project has maintained an MIT license since 2023 and has accumulated over a million downloads. Its architecture is designed so that nothing is installed or fetched unless explicitly requested.

🧩 Core Capabilities

The node library supports a wide range of processing tasks, including:

  • Tiled and affine samplers, noise shaping, shift and schedule control, model quantizing, and LoRA stacks.
  • Crop-and-restore edits, edit regions, and specific model integrations like MiniMax H3 Image, Fibo 2.0, and BluePixel 4K.
  • Raw-style develop, film stocks, darkroom effects, and looks baked into LUTs.
  • Levels, LUTs, ACES and colour spaces, linear light, HDR video, and scopes and charts.
  • Skin, face, and subject masks, including masks drawn directly on the picture and subjects followed through a clip.
  • Filters and optics, layer stacks, layered PSD and TIFF files, and ControlNet preprocessors.

🎬 Video and 3D Features

Recent developments extend ComfyUI’s utility into complex video production and 3D generation:

  • Video Production: The Prompt Timeline allows long videos to be built a segment at a time. Features include upscaling, sparse attention, and Pika H3 Flex integration. The system supports video with sound, video super-resolution of any length, edits, transitions, titles, restored footage, face restoration through a shot, audio mixing, and beats.
  • 3D Generation: Capabilities include scenes, generated models, characters, meshes, blockouts, point cloud worlds, and Video Blueprint.

📚 Text and Logic Tools

The platform also includes utilities for prompt engineering and data handling:

  • Prompt terminology and a style library.
  • A system prompt library.
  • Support for text, lists, and dictionaries.

🚀 Availability and Resources

  • License: MIT (since 2023).
  • Downloads: Over a million.
  • Examples: 144 example workflows are provided.
  • Installation Model: Nothing installed, nothing fetched unless asked.

#ComfyUI #AIWorkflows #VideoGeneration #3DGeneration #OpenSource

Source: WASasquatch/was-node-suite-comfyui

item.title: ComfyUI LayerStyle Advance Adds Photoshop‑Like Layering Features

🔍 Overview

  • Migrates basic Photoshop functions to ComfyUI.
  • Nodes are split into repositories to reduce dependency problems.

🧩 How it Works

item.title: myAiVideos: An open-source pipeline for automated Chinese short-video production
item.description:
myAiVideos: An open-source pipeline for automated Chinese short-video production

myAiVideos is a new open-source engineering project designed for the automated production of Chinese-language short videos. It covers the full pipeline from topic discovery through creative generation, visuals, audio, and post-production, all the way to distribution.

🔍 Overview

The system is built as a modular platform that coordinates multiple AI models to handle generation and quality gating. Its architecture is designed to be decoupled, allowing individual layers of the pipeline to be independently replaced.

🧩 How it works

The project utilizes a seven-layer pipeline architecture:

  • L1: Topic
  • L2: Creative
  • L3: Visual
  • L4: Audio
  • L5: Post-production
  • L6: Distribution
  • L7: Optimization

Orchestration is managed by a FastAPI core, while a Java gateway acts as the platform governance layer. The gateway handles authentication, routing, circuit breaking, metering, and observability. Key technical mechanisms include:

  • Multi-model failover: The Java gateway aggregates DeepSeek, Qwen, and GLM using Resilience4j protection to automatically rotate failed providers.
  • Prompt anchoring: Maintains the visual identity of subjects across video segments.
  • CLIP gating: Rejects off-prompt keyframes early using text-image consistency checks.
  • Audio-video sync rescue: Employs a four-tier strategy involving audio tempo adjustments, video padding, and narration rewrites.

⚙️ Key details

The system provides full-stack observability by propagating trace_id across Java and Python environments and offering Langfuse call-tree visibility. Metering and rate limiting are handled via an AOP aspect that captures token and cost data without requiring code changes, aggregated by tenant. The production-ready setup includes SSE progress streaming, single-segment regeneration, and rolling log archives.

Component Technology / Model
Gateway Spring Boot 3.5, WebClient, Resilience4j, Caffeine, Prometheus
Text LLM DeepSeek
Multimodal Moderation Zhipu GLM-4V
Visuals Kling v2.5
Speech Synthesis Volcengine / MiniMax TTS
Transcription faster-whisper

🚀 Availability

myAiVideos is available as an open-source engineering project. It supports local execution using Docker Desktop version 24 or higher. Node.js 20 or higher is required for frontend development, while Python 3.11 or higher is needed for local execution without Docker or for running host tests. Health endpoints are available for the Python API, Java Gateway, and Frontend.

#OpenSource #VideoGeneration #FastAPI #Java #AIModels

Source: myccarl/ai-shortVideo-pipeline

item.title: QLC+ Is a Free, Cross-Platform Open-Source Lighting Control Tool
item.description:
QLC+ Is a Free, Cross-Platform Open-Source Lighting Control Tool

QLC+ is a free, open-source, and cross-platform software designed to control DMX and analog lighting systems. It is a fork of the original QLC project and aims to continue development while introducing new features to reach the level of available commercial software.

📝 Overview

QLC+ is powerful and user-friendly software that supports a wide range of lighting hardware, including moving heads, dimmers, and scanners. It is designed for use in live shows, theatre, architectural installations, and venues, empowering both experienced professionals and beginners to take control of their lighting fixtures.

🧩 How It Works

The software supports multiple lighting control protocols, including DMX, Art-Net, and sACN. While the master branch is kept free of critical errors, users who regularly update the source code via git pull may occasionally encounter compiler warnings, errors, or unresolved symbols due to dependencies between objects, which can sometimes require a full package recompilation.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Licensing & Cost: Free and open-source.
  • Protocols: DMX, Art-Net, sACN.
  • Community Support: A dedicated forum is available to submit new fixtures, give feedback, and share new ideas.
  • Documentation: Official documentation is provided to explain specific features of QLC+.
  • Issue Tracking: A badge is available to view currently confirmed issues, and compilation guides along with platform-specific instructions are hosted in the GitHub Wiki.

🚀 Availability

QLC+ runs on the following operating systems:

  • Linux
  • Windows (10 and later)
  • macOS (10.12 and later)
  • Raspberry Pi

A dedicated support page is available to help users find assistance and resolve potential issues.

#LightingControl #OpenSource #QLC+ #DMX #Theatre

Source: mcallegari/qlcplus

item.title: Stable Baselines3 declared stable with focus on maintenance
item.description:
Stable Baselines3 declared stable with focus on maintenance

Stable Baselines3 (SB3) has reached a stable state as most features from the original roadmap have been implemented. Development focus has shifted to bug fixes and maintenance, including documentation updates and user experience improvements, while newer algorithms continue to be developed in associated repositories.

🔍 Overview

Stable Baselines3 is a set of reliable implementations of reinforcement learning algorithms in PyTorch. It is the next major version of Stable Baselines. The toolset is designed to be simple for beginners to experiment with advanced RL concepts without being buried in implementation details, though it assumes some prior knowledge about Reinforcement Learning.

🧩 How it works

The algorithms are intended to make it easier for the research community and industry to replicate, refine, and identify new ideas. They serve as baselines to build projects on top of and as a tool for comparing new approaches against existing ones. The performance of each algorithm was tested, and detailed logs and reports are provided on the OpenRL Benchmark platform.

⚙️ Key details

  • Core Library: SB3 provides reliable PyTorch implementations of RL algorithms.
  • Associated Repositories:
    • SB3 Contrib: Newer algorithms are regularly added here.
    • SBX: Faster variants are developed in this SB3 + Jax repository.
    • RL Zoo: An active training framework with its own roadmap.
  • Integrations: SB3 includes integrations with Weights & Biases for experiment tracking and Hugging Face for storing and sharing trained models.
  • Migration: A migration guide from SB2 to SB3 is available in the documentation.

🚀 Availability

Documentation is available online at https://stable-baselines3.readthedocs.io/. Detailed presentations of SB3 can be found in the v1.0 blog post or the associated JMLR paper. RL Baselines3 Zoo, part of the ecosystem, provides scripts for training, evaluating agents, tuning hyperparameters, plotting results, and recording videos. It also includes a collection of tuned hyperparameters for common environments and RL algorithms, along with agents trained with those settings, providing a simple interface to train and enjoy RL agents and benchmark different algorithms.

#ReinforcementLearning #PyTorch #StableBaselines3 #MLOps #OpenSource

Source: DLR-RM/stable-baselines3

item.title: agent_learning: An Open-Source AI Agent Development Textbook
item.description:
agent_learning: An Open-Source AI Agent Development Textbook

An open-source AI Agent textbook and learning repository called agent_learning has been released to address the skill gap between calling an LLM API and building a complete Agent system. The resource provides a systematic tutorial covering the full lifecycle of agent development, from foundational concepts to production deployment.

🧩 How it works

The textbook is structured to guide developers through the core components of agentic systems. It covers the transition from basic capabilities to advanced deployment strategies, including:

  • Core Capabilities: Function calling, memory systems, planning, RAG, and context engineering.
  • Advanced Topics: Agentic RL, multi-agent systems, and self-evolving agents.
  • Production Readiness: Evaluation, security, and deployment pipelines.

The curriculum includes 26 chapters organized across six main areas: foundations, core capabilities, frameworks, multi-agent systems, production, and capstone projects. The material bridges theoretical papers and practical application by providing explanations for techniques such as ReAct, Reflexion, MemGPT/Letta, GraphRAG, and GRPO.

⚙️ Key details

The repository is designed for bilingual accessibility and includes substantial visual aids to support complex concepts.

Feature Description
Language Support English and Chinese editions with matching tables of contents
Visual Resources 330+ original SVG diagrams and 5 interactive demos
Practical Baseline reference-agent/ folder with a runnable baseline including tools, memory, and security gates
Code Structure Separate sources for English (src/en/) and Chinese (src/zh/) mdBooks

The chapter structure includes specific deep dives into:

  • Frameworks: LangChain, LangGraph, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, Claude Code, and OpenCode V2.
  • Techniques: Harness Engineering, Skills, and Context Engineering.
  • Advanced Systems: Multimodal Agents and DeepSeek Harness.

💡 Why it matters

The agent_learning repository is explicitly designed for developers who have moved past simple API integration and need to build, evaluate, secure, and deploy Agent systems. By combining theoretical paper-to-practice explanations with runnable code baselines and interactive demos, it serves as a comprehensive reference for both individual developers and teams looking to standardize their AI agent development workflows.

#AIAgents #OpenSource #LLM #RAG #LangChain #DeveloperEducation

Source: Haozhe-Xing/agent_learning

item.title: Laminar Enables Scalable Asynchronous RL Post-Training for LLMs
item.description:
Laminar Enables Scalable Asynchronous RL Post-Training for LLMs

Laminar is a scalable reinforcement learning post‑training framework that enables large language models and long‑horizon agents to be fine‑tuned at scale.

🔍 Overview

  • Built on verl and Uni-Agent.
  • Open‑source implementation of Laminar: A Scalable Asynchronous RL Post‑Training Framework (EuroSys ’26).
  • Decoupled, asynchronous, and fault‑tolerant design for large‑cluster scaling.

🧩 How it Works

  • Fully decoupled training and rollout: independent loops via data and weight planes.
  • Data plane (ExperienceBuffer) buffers completed trajectories for AsyncRLTrainer.
  • Weight plane (Relay) stages published weights for inference replicas to pull on demand.
  • Trajectory‑level asynchrony: generates and consumes individual trajectories independently.
  • Version‑mixed partial rollout: interrupts in‑flight generations on weight sync and continues with newer weights.
  • Version‑consistent rollout: keeps each trajectory on a single model version.
  • Dynamic repack: consolidates long‑tail trajectories onto fewer replicas, freeing drained replicas to pull the latest weights.
  • Concurrent multi‑checkpoint evaluation (laminar.eval): version‑pinned routing and tail repacking for bubble‑free offline batch and online streaming evaluation.
  • Fault‑tolerant execution: prevents single‑replica failures from stalling cluster‑wide progress.
  • Inference engines recover failed replicas from Relay or checkpoint storage while preserving in‑flight trajectory prefixes.
  • Trainer engine resumes from the latest checkpoint (asynchronous per‑step checkpoint in progress).

⚙️ Key Details

  • Extras
1
2
3
4

--extra vllm vLLM rollout and evaluation backend
--extra megatron Megatron‑LM training backend
--extra fsdp FSDP2 training backend
--extra ucx UCX transport for Relay (recommended)

🚀 Availability

  • Open‑source on GitHub (built on verl and Uni-Agent).
  • Manages Python, CUDA, wheel indexes, and pinned Git dependencies with uv (see pyproject.toml and uv.lock).

💡 Why it Matters

  • In SWE agent training (Qwen3‑Coder‑30B‑A3B‑Instruct on SWE‑rebench, evaluated on SWE‑bench Verified on 64×H800) it improved resolve rate from 46.6 % to 52.2 %, surpassing the baseline peak of 51.4 %.
  • Uses 33 % fewer trained samples and 64 % fewer GPU‑hours to exceed the baseline peak.

#Laminar #ReinforcementLearning #LargeLanguageModels #OpenSource

Source: verl-project/laminar

item.title: LORE: An open-source AI reader that builds knowledge graphs from e-books with citation support
item.description:
LORE: An open-source AI reader that builds knowledge graphs from e-books with citation support

LORE is an open-source AI reader that transforms e-books into interactive knowledge graphs, answering questions with every sentence cited and respecting the user’s reading progress without revealing later spoilers.

📚 What LORE Does

LORE turns each book into a knowledge graph of its characters, places, groups and events, then answers questions from the text itself. Every sentence in an answer cites the passage it comes from, and a second pass checks each citation against that passage and removes anything the book doesn’t say.

🔍 How It Tracks Progress

Users can set their reading progress per book, and all outputs—answers, the graph, character profiles, and timelines—stop at the specified chapter. This is enforced at retrieval, ensuring the model never sees what comes later in the book.

🧩 Key Features

  • Answers questions about characters, places, and events
  • Provides character profiles, story timelines, and relationship maps
  • Supports long, sectioned analyses with full citations
  • Click any character for detailed profiles with passage-backed information
  • Handles tracking character changes across multiple books
  • Manages complex world and magic system explanations

⚙️ Technical Implementation

LORE uses Gemini (free tier works), Claude, or OpenAI for reading and writing; embeddings run locally on Ollama. An MCP server enables integration with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and other MCP clients to search libraries and ask questions.

Users can choose their AI model on the admin page, with options including self-hosted models like llama.cpp’s llama-server, vLLM, LM Studio, or Ollama. Each person added to the system gets their own private library.

🚀 Availability and Setup

Self-hosting requires Python 3.12+, uv, Node.js 18+, and Ollama. The local embedding model is installed via ollama pull nomic-embed-text. A Gemini API key (or Claude/OpenAI key) is required, which can be stored in an environment variable or in ~/.config/lore/gemini.env.

The fastest option is the hosted beta at lore.jrvn.site, where new accounts start with A Study in Scarlet already processed for immediate use. Setup involves opening the app, adding books via EPUB or PDF, and waiting for processing to complete.

💡 Integration Options

LORE runs an MCP server, allowing Claude to search the library and ask questions with reading position constraints. The hosted beta integrates at claude.ai via Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector using https://lore.jrvn.site/mcp. Self-hosted instances run through uv run lore mcp (stdio) or uv run lore mcp --http.

#AIreader #knowledgegraph #OpenSource #ebooks #MCP #citations

Source: Jatin-Roopchandani/LORE

item.title: Pydantic Deep Agents: Open‑Source, Self‑Hosted AI Assistant and Framework
item.description:
Pydantic Deep Agents: Open‑Source, Self‑Hosted AI Assistant and Framework

Pydantic Deep Agents releases an open‑source terminal AI assistant and Python framework. It lets you point any model—Claude, GPT, Gemini, or a local model—to the same harness.

🔍 Overview

Pydantic Deep Agents is an open‑source, self‑hosted terminal AI assistant and Python framework. It lets you point any model—Claude, GPT, Gemini, or a local model—to the same harness.

🧩 How it works

  • The assistant runs on Pydantic AI.
  • It can plan, edit files, run shell commands, search the web, remember across sessions, spawn sub‑agents, and connect to MCP servers.
  • The single function call create_deep_agent() provides a model with a filesystem, shell, planning, memory, sub‑agents, sandboxed execution, MCP, and unlimited context.
  • Live Run Forking splits a single run into parallel branches; an AI judge merges the branches back together.
  • When an agent faces a decision point (e.g. “should I refactor this with a decorator or a context manager?” ), the fork‑and‑merge mechanism allows exploring both options.

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Type safety 100 % type‑safe
License MIT for the assistant and framework; Apache‑2.0 for Agenticos
Model support Claude, GPT, Gemini, local
Runtime Self‑hosted terminal AI assistant
Harness Same code used for the single‑function create_deep_agent()

🚀 Availability

  • Install it locally and point it at any model.
  • Use it today, or ship your own agent in one function call.
  • The repo contains both the terminal assistant and the Python framework.

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a unified, open‑source alternative to commercial assistants like Claude Code.
  • Enables teams to use a sovereign, self‑hosted AI layer with budgets, approvals, guardrails, and activity tracking via Agenticos by Vstorm.
  • The fork‑and‑merge runtime supports parallel reasoning paths, giving developers more flexibility when designing agent behavior.

#AIagents #OpenSource #Python #Pydantic

Source: vstorm-co/pydantic-deepagents

item.title: Python SDKs for MCP Toolbox Enable Gen AI Integration
item.description:

🔍 Overview

These SDKs are designed to seamlessly integrate the functionalities of the MCP Toolbox into Gen AI applications. They allow you to load tools defined in Toolbox and use them as standard Python functions or objects within popular orchestration frameworks or your custom code.

🧩 Packages

item.title: Autumn-27 ARTEX Open-Source Fork Now Maintained by ChainReactors
item.description:
Autumn-27 ARTEX Open-Source Fork Now Maintained by ChainReactors

The Autumn-27/ARTEX project, an AI autonomous penetration testing system originally built with a Go backend and Next.js frontend, has seen its open-source continuation. The repository RuoJi6/ARTEX is a fork of the original Autumn-27/ARTEX, preserving the upstream commit history and AGPL-3.0 license. It is now maintained by ChainReactors.

🧩 How it works

The system integrates with external data sources to streamline asset collection. Specifically, it supports direct synchronization of asset data from ScopeSentry, eliminating the need for manual repeated collection. Users configure the ScopeSentry address and API key on the “Asset Sync” page, select targets and asset types (such as domains, subdomains, IPs, ports, sites, or endpoints) by project or task dimension, and import data to merge it into the ARTEX asset graph for agent exploration.

⚙️ Key details

  • Database & LLM: The system depends on PostgreSQL and requires an LLM configuration for exploration, supporting either ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY (configurable via CLI or UI).
  • MCP Support: Remote MCP can be configured in system settings using http (Streamable HTTP) or sse (legacy SSE).
  • Dockerization: The ruoji6/artex Docker image is built and published via GitHub Actions. It includes common tools like ripgrep, curl, vim, npm, and nmap. The image supports linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 architectures, with Docker automatically selecting the matching host architecture.
  • Persistence: The ./skills and ./data directories are persisted via bind mounts.

🚀 Availability

  • Docker Setup: The installation script automatically detects and installs Docker. Users can choose between “All Docker” (which generates a .env file and runs docker compose up -d) or local compilation.
  • Local Setup: For local runs, users select a database option, generate a config.json, and compile an embedded single binary.
  • Access: After installation, the service is accessible at http://localhost:8787, requiring an initial setup at /setup to set the admin password.
  • Download: Release packages are available for download from the repository’s Releases page. Linux ARM64 users (including ARM64 Kali) should select the linux-arm64 build, while x86_64 users select linux-amd64.
  • Execution: Users must launch the application using start.sh or start.bat rather than running ./artex directly. These scripts act as daemons that restart the program based on exit codes, which is required for the “one-click update” feature to function correctly.

#ARTEX #PenetrationTesting #OpenSource #SecurityTools #ChainReactors

Source: RuoJi6/ARTEX

item.title: Dograh Launches Fully Open‑Source Voice AI Platform with One‑Click Self‑Hosting
item.description:
Dograh Launches Fully Open‑Source Voice AI Platform with One‑Click Self‑Hosting

Dograh, an open‑source voice AI platform, is now available as a self‑hosted alternative to Vapi and Retell.

🔍 Overview

  • 100% open source and self‑hostable, eliminating vendor lock‑in.
  • Licensed under the BSD 2‑Clause license.
  • Maintained by YC alumni and exit founders who are committed to keeping voice AI open.

🧩 How It Works

  • Visual workflow builder enables building and testing production voice agents in minutes.
  • MCP native support lets AI coding assistants help design and edit agents.
  • One‑click self‑hosting: run a single Docker command to get the platform up in about 60 seconds. 
    1
2

    curl -o docker-compose.yaml https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dograh-hq/dograh/main/docker-compose.yaml
curl -o start_docker.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dograh-hq/dograh/main/scripts/start_docker.sh
  • Remote deployment is supported via documentation.

⚙️ Key Details

  • BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) across Speech‑to‑Speech, LLM, STT, and TTS.
  • Flexible integration with any LLM, STT, or TTS provider, or use Dograh’s own stack.
  • Full source‑level customization – every line of code is open and modifiable.
  • Data residency is under your control: your infrastructure, your rules.
  • Pricing: free for self‑hosted use; cloud usage is billed on a usage‑based model.
  • Telemetry is optional; it can be disabled by setting ENABLE_TELEMETRY=false before startup.

🚀 Availability

item.title: New Fine-Tunes Enable Iberian Language Variety Control in Multilingual Translation
item.description:
New Fine-Tunes Enable Iberian Language Variety Control in Multilingual Translation

Researchers have introduced new fine-tuned variants of the MADLAD-400-3B-MT multilingual translation model that add control over regional language varieties, particularly for Spanish dialects and minoritized languages of the Iberian Peninsula. The work addresses a key limitation where existing massively multilingual models typically provide only one tag per language with poor coverage of regional varieties and smaller languages.

🧩 How it works

The team created three fine-tuned versions of the base model using low-rank adaptation (LoRA), back-translation of monolingual text, and replay of the base model’s own translations:

  • Each variant introduces new target tags to control language varieties
  • For Spanish varieties: <2es_ES> for Spanish as written in Spain and <2es_419> for Latin American Spanish
  • One unified model handles three Romance languages: Asturian (<2ast>), Aragonese (<2an>), and Aranese (<2oc_aranes>)

⚙️ Key details

The Spanish variety models required careful data curation:

  • Annotated 250.9 million documents from MADLAD-400’s Spanish split with a Spain vs. Latin America classifier
  • Applied selection rules that excluded Latin American documents from a 340-document reference set

Performance results show significant improvements:

Model Vocabulary Matching Vosotros Usage chrF++ Improvement
Castilian (base) 62% 10% -
Castilian (fine-tuned) 97% 70% Improved

The researchers discovered a phenomenon called “tag collapse” where new tags initialized from parent language tags drift toward the new variety (84-87% identical outputs). The Iberian model used contrastive pairs and separate learning rates for tag embeddings to maintain tag distinctiveness.

For the Iberian Peninsula model:

  • Trained using publicly available data, mostly TAN-IBE Wikipedia corpora
  • Matches or beats TAN-IBE Marian systems in four of six Spanish directions on FLORES+
  • 1.9 BLEU behind in Spanish→Aranese (attributed to written variety differences, not quality)
  • Second only to SalamandraTA-7B in most directions

⚠️ Trade-offs

All three fine-tuned models experience a 0.6-0.7 chrF++ decrease on average across thirteen other FLORES-200 translation directions, representing a trade-off between improved regional variety handling and reduced performance in other language pairs.

🚀 Availability

The models, training data, and variety classifier are released under open licences for public use.

#machinetranslation #multilingualAI #languagevarieties #opensource

Source: Teaching a Multilingual Translation Model Regional Varieties: Castilian and Latin American Spanish, Asturian, Aragonese and Aranese with MADLAD-400-3B-MT

item.title: GitHub Builds AI-Powered Conference Badge for Hands-On Learning
item.description:
GitHub Builds AI-Powered Conference Badge for Hands-On Learning

🎮 Playful Hacking at GitHub Universe

For the last four years at GitHub Universe, we’ve had hackable conference badges. What started as a simple e-ink display for your name and job title morphed into a labor of love for Martin Woodward, VP of Developer Relations. This year, the badge evolved into a device with a color screen, rechargeable battery, accelerometer sensors, and touch-sensitive gaming controls.

🤖 AI Accelerates Code Creation

According to the Octoverse report, 40% of pull requests were started by agents by September. That’s a big jump from the 17% we saw in March, which was already a pretty high number. AI can turn our ideas into working code faster than ever before.

🏃 Learning Through Building

At the GitHub Universe closing keynote, Martin wanted to teach himself machine learning, so he built himself a pedometer onto his conference badge. He used Copilot to collect movement data from the badge’s accelerometer, trained a simple machine-learning model in his browser, and deployed it to the badge. Then he walked around to test whether it could tell the difference between walking, standing still, and fidgeting.

⚖️ Balancing Innovation and Open Source Values

We’re seeing maintainers get absolutely hammered with AI-powered contributions to their repositories, which adds a lot to the maintenance burden. As Martin explained in the keynote, “Open source is the freedom to inspect, to remix, and to share without asking for permission. But it’s not the freedom to impose your will on others.”

🎮 Gaming on the Badge

We answered the perennial question on our badge, “But can it run Doom?” Why yes, yes it does.

📣 Getting Your Own Badge

Plus, use code FREESHIPBLOG26 for free standard shipping through December 1, 2026. We made some extra badges just for you. Order yours today, then tell us what you’ll be building.

#AI #OpenSource #MachineLearning #GitHub

Source: Art of play in the age of AI

item.title: HY-World 1.5: Real-Time Interactive World Modeling
item.description:
HY-World 1.5: Real-Time Interactive World Modeling

We are excited to announce the release of HY-World 1.5 (WorldPlay), the first open-source, real-time interactive, and long-term geometrically consistent world model. This breakthrough bridges the gap between immersive 3D world generation and real-time interaction, resolving the trade-off between speed and memory that limits current methods.

🔍 Overview

  • HY-World 1.5 is a state-of-the-art 3D world model.
  • It enables real-time, interactive world modeling with long-term geometric consistency.
  • The model is based on a streaming video diffusion model, WorldPlay.

🧩 How it works

  • HY-World 1.5 draws power from four key designs.
  • It uses a Dual Action Representation to enable robust interaction.

⚙️ Key details

  • HY-World 1.5 resolves the trade-off between speed and memory.
  • It is the first open-source, real-time interactive, and long-term geometrically consistent world model.

🚀 Availability

  • We release the training code for WorldPlay-8B model, enabling the community to train and fine-tune their own world models.
  • We release the RL post-training code WorldCompass for WorldPlay-8B model.
  • We open-source WorldPlay-5B model, a new lightweight model that fits into small-VRAM GPUs.
  • We update the inference code with quantization and engineering optimization for even faster inference speeds.
  • We present the technical report and research paper of HY-World 1.5 (WorldPlay).

💡 Why it matters

  • HY-World 1.5 bridges the gap between immersive 3D world generation and real-time interaction.
  • It resolves the trade-off between speed and memory that limits current methods.

item.title: Idun Agent Platform Is No Longer Maintained as Open-Source Project
item.description:
Idun Agent Platform Is No Longer Maintained as Open-Source Project

The Idun Agent Platform is no longer maintained. Its code stays open source under the GPLv3 license, and its official documentation remains online for reference.

🔍 Overview

Idun Agent Platform was created as an open-source, self-hosted production wrapper for LangGraph and Google ADK agents. It allows developers to deploy agents as production-ready FastAPI services without vendor lock-in.

Teams building AI agents typically face a tradeoff: building a custom production wrapper (combining FastAPI, traces, guardrails, and an admin UI), which is slow, or adopting SaaS solutions like LangGraph Cloud or LangSmith, which introduces sovereignty trade-offs. Idun provided a third path by offering a self-sufficient FastAPI process installed via a single pip install command on local or private infrastructure.

⚙️ Key details

The platform is distributed as a single wheel bundling three Python packages:

Package Description
idun_agent_engine The engine SDK providing the FastAPI app factory, Model Context Protocol (MCP) registry, observability, and guardrails.
idun_agent_standalone Provides the idun CLI, admin REST API, and UIs for chat, administration, and traces.
idun_agent_schema Contains the Pydantic configuration schemas.

Built-in platform capabilities and features include:

  • AG-UI copilotkit API and bundled chat UI
  • Admin panel and managed prompts
  • 15+ guardrails
  • MCP tool governance
  • OpenTelemetry observability and dedicated trace store
  • OIDC and SSO integration
  • Memory persistence and messaging integrations

🛠️ Usage details

  • Prerequisites: Python 3.12 or 3.13.
  • Installation: pip install idun-agent-engine.
  • CLI: The idun executable provides commands including setup, serve, init, hash-password, and agent serve via idun_agent_standalone.
  • Workflow: Users create a directory (such as my-agent/), save the required files, and run the engine from within that directory or via an absolute path.
  • Path Resolution: The graph_definition: "./agent.py:graph" setting is resolved relative to the directory where idun init is run.
  • Endpoints: Launching the service opens a chat UI at http://localhost:8000. Settings, MCP servers, guardrails, and SSO are configured at /admin, while trace data is available at /admin/traces.

🚀 Availability

  • Maintenance Status: No longer maintained.
  • Licensing: Code remains available open source under GPLv3.
  • Documentation: Stays online for developer reference.

#LangGraph #FastAPI #OpenSource #AIAgents #Python

Source: Idun-Group/idun-agent-platform

item.title: Music gear companies open-source devices in response to AI vibe-coding
item.description:
Music gear companies open-source devices in response to AI vibe-coding

The emergence of powerful vibe-coding agents and tools has created chaos in the music gear world, forcing companies to determine how to respond to a wave of AI-aided custom firmwares and modding communities. While some manufacturers have remained silent, others have decided to embrace the trend by opening up their devices and providing tools for the community.

🔍 Overview

As it became clear that no piece of music gear was safe from AI tools and curious tinkerers, companies began making their devices open source. Major names like inMusic, the parent company of Akai, Moog, and Native Instruments, decided to “join ’em” rather than resist. Meanwhile, companies like Roland, Korg, Arturia, and Novation have yet to issue public statements on the matter.

⚙️ Key details

  • inMusic: inMusic CEO Jack O’Donnell stated the company will provide a toolbox and the inner workings of devices like the MPC or Sample so people can do what they want. This includes a recently launched SDK and several open-source devices, including the recently teased MPC Sample Key. Akai aims to walk a fine line by offering modders access while keeping products reliable for professionals, promising a “reset button” so users can experiment without losing their original setup.
  • Behringer: The company announced a slew of open-source devices, including a $150 clone of the MPC One called Kick, a clone of the E-mu SP-1200, the Anima DJ controller, the Ignite sequencer, and the Polykeys 61 MIDI controller. Launch dates for these products are currently unclear.
  • M-Vave: The company’s $70 pocketable clone of the Yamaha DX7 became popular due to its price and hackability, leading to more than a dozen custom firmwares. M-Vave responded by releasing an open-source firmware for developers and confirmed its successor, the FM-2, will also be open source.
  • Erica Synths: The company released the source code for its LXR-02 drum machine. Founder Ģirts Ozoliņš noted the sustainability of using one device with various options instead of buying multiple “plastic boxes,” while acknowledging that vibe coding does not offset the environmental impact of data centers.
  • Polyend: Open-sourced its line of Tracker grooveboxes and released the Endless guitar pedal last year, which allows users to vibe-code their own effects.
  • Elektron: The company banned links to custom firmware from its official forums, warning that modifications could brick machines, prevent updates, or affect warranty coverage. CPO Christian Alsing stated that while he is sympathetic to the hacker community and believes users have the right to modify their devices, he pushed back on accusations that the company is withholding features.

💡 Why it matters

The shift toward open-sourcing hardware and firmware reflects a strategic pivot in the music technology industry. Companies are balancing the potential for community innovation and sustainability against the risks of hardware instability and the environmental costs associated with AI development.

#vibe-coding #open-source #music-gear #firmware #modding

Source: Has vibe coding made open source the new normal for synths?

item.title: OpenQodex adds pre-push code review for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor
item.description:
OpenQodex adds pre-push code review for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor

Open source code review tool OpenQodex now runs inside coding agents to check every change before you push. It operates without requiring a separate account or API key, acting as a separate reviewer that validates code changes made by agents in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Cline.

🔍 Overview

  • OpenQodex is an open source code review tool for coding agents.
  • It runs a separate reviewer that checks every change an agent writes before the user pushes.
  • No account or key of its own is required.
  • It is available for use in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Cline.

🧩 How it works

  • Code Graph: A code graph provides the agent with a map of the codebase.
  • Scanner Integration: It runs scanners that fit the changed files, keeping findings on the changed lines. A scanner is a program that checks code without a model, such as gitleaks or semgrep.
  • Dependency Check: Every supported lockfile in the repository is checked against osv.dev at every review and scan of a change. Advisories outside the changed lines are shown but never counted.
  • Fresh Reviewers: Separate Claude Code or Codex processes on the user’s login run the review, with no memory of the current session.
  • Verification: A script checks every line a reviewer quotes as evidence against the code. Verifiers confirm or refute every candidate and every scanner finding.

⚙️ Key details

  • Initiation: Users say to their agent, “review my change with openqodex”.
  • Setup: The init command finds agents on the machine, lists the files it will write, and asks for confirmation once.
  • Terminal Execution: In your own terminal, run ~/.openqodex/bin/openqodex review.
  • Sandbox Limitation: In its default sandbox, Codex gives commands no network, so the terminal command must be run outside the sandbox.
  • Scope: The review covers commits not yet pushed plus everything uncommitted.
  • Output: The tool prints a receipt with the verdict, one line per finding, and the path to report.html. It also writes report.md, report.json, and report.sarif.

🚀 Availability

  • Works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Cline, and Goose.
  • The host identifier can be claude-code, codex, cursor, cline, or goose.
  • An npx install does not put OpenQodex on the system PATH.
  • The reviewer was tested with Claude Code 2.1.330 using claude-opus-5-5.

#OpenQodex #CodeReview #AIagents #ClaudeCode #OpenSource

Source: openqodex/openqodex

item.title: Analysis of 5,400 Malicious NPM Packages Reveals Evolving Supply Chain Tactics
item.description:
Analysis of 5,400 Malicious NPM Packages Reveals Evolving Supply Chain Tactics

In this first part, we analyzed approximately 5,400 confirmed malicious npm packages published between December 2025 and October 2026, the first year following npm’s revocation of long-lived authentication tokens. The dataset comprises packages detected by a scanner that analyzes npm publish events for suspicious packages, with results filtered for precision by retaining only packages with at least one independent source, such as a public advisory, a vendor-published campaign report, an npm security takedown, or analyst review. Time is measured by npm publish date, and the unit of record is the package version, dated by its first malicious version.

🔍 Threat Landscape Overview

Monthly counts of confirmed malicious packages vary by a factor of fifteen across the period. Activity remains stable with several hundred new publisher accounts per month and a flat rate of malicious packages relative to total packages published. In August 2026, a single dependency-confusion campaign accounts for 78% of confirmed versions. Dependency-confusion reconnaissance is continuous, present in every month at a consistent level, while compromise of legitimate packages is episodic.

🧩 Attack Vectors and Campaigns

Three waves of a single worm family occurred in May, June, and August 2026. The May and August waves each compromised more than one hundred packages, and the June wave republished a vendor’s entire scope in one day.

  • Token Theft Shift: Classic long-lived tokens were revoked on December 9, 2025. Theft of npm authentication tokens peaked at 22% of packages in March 2026 and fell below 5% from May. The tokens targeted in this period were plausibly granular access tokens and CI secrets.
  • Obfuscation: The share of actors whose packages trigger an obfuscation rule more than doubled between May and August 2026. 72% of packages have an obfuscation marker, and 30% retrieve a second stage.
  • Compromised Packages: 78% of compromised versions add or modify a lifecycle script, compared with 4% of attacker-created packages. 23% show a change of maintainer or publisher, but the majority of compromises are published through the legitimate account and leave ownership records unchanged.

⚙️ Attacker Profile and Package Characteristics

99% of malicious packages are published by single-maintainer accounts, and 55% of accounts use a free-mail address. Two-thirds of accounts publish exactly one malicious package; among those publishing more than one, the median interval from first to last malicious publish is under one day.

  • DPRK-nexus Campaigns: These are the exception, operating several hundred accounts at one to two packages each, with 83% on free-mail addresses.
  • Other Named Campaigns: These use free-mail addresses in 15% of cases, consistent with procured account pools.
  • Package Traits: 88% of packages are under thirty days old at the malicious publish, 75% declare no repository, and 65% retain npm init template values in the author, description, or repository fields. 54% declare a lifecycle script, and 17% carry an internal-looking name (core, utils, sdk, config). Typosquatting is a minority tactic, with 13% embedding a popular package name and under 5% being within two character edits of one.

💡 Payload Behavior and Targeting

Credential and data theft is the predominant behavior in every month, except August. In August, a significant number of packages stole credentials but ultimately aimed to deliver a Sliver command-and-control implant on the victim machine, changing their classification to Trojan / Downloader.

  • Credential Targets: 45% of credential stealers target a single credential class, while 36% target three or more. Single-class stealers are distributed evenly across cloud credentials, SSH keys, AI-developer credentials, npm tokens, and .env files. In multi-class stealers, cloud credentials, SSH keys, and .env files co-occur; wallet and browser-data theft occur separately.
  • AI Developer Credentials: Targeting remained at 1-4% of packages throughout the year, but absolute counts rose with volume. AI-developer credentials are the most specialized target: 80% of packages that target them target no other class.
  • OS Specificity: 55% of packages contain no operating-system-specific code. Droppers target Windows (PowerShell, scheduled tasks, executables), while credential stealers and backdoors target Linux (systemd, cron, shell configuration files). macOS-specific code appears in approximately one in eight stealers.
  • Scoped Packages: 24% of packages are scoped, across more than three hundred distinct scopes, most of which contain a single malicious package.

#npmSecurity #SupplyChainAttack #MalwareAnalysis #ThreatIntelligence #OpenSource

Source: What 5,400 Malicious npm Packages Reveal about Software Supply Chain Risk in 2026

item.title: FineEnvs: An Open-Source Resource for End-to-End RL Environments
item.description:
FineEnvs: An Open-Source Resource for End-to-End RL Environments

A new open-source resource called FineEnvs has been released to address the shifting bottleneck in reinforcement learning (RL) for LLMs, where the environment design now poses a greater challenge than the algorithm. The project provides an end-to-end, reproducible, and open-source framework for designing, building, deploying, training against, and scaling RL environments to thousands of concurrent sessions.

🧩 How it works

The ecosystem is built on real, executable code rather than diagrams or unverified examples. Key characteristics of the resource include:

  • Reproducible Training: Every rollout has been executed, and every training curve comes from a job that users can launch in a single command without requiring their own GPU.
  • Comprehensive Coverage: The resource covers how to design an environment, how to build it, how to deploy it, how to train against it, and how to scale it to thousands of concurrent sessions.
  • Framework Agnosticism: The environments are compatible with six different frameworks, allowing users to train using SETA, native OpenCode, or Harbor, utilizing HF Jobs or Slurm.
  • Verified SFT Traces: Includes data-analysis tasks with verified SFT traces and a single-turn GRPO tutorial on HF Jobs.

⚙️ Key details

The release features three distinct environments demonstrated across six frameworks side by side. These environments utilize specific models and reward mechanisms:

Environment / Task Description Model / Reward Mechanism
Math Image OCR Train models to read math images into LaTeX Qwen3-VL-2B with a verifiable reward
Watercolour Painting Train models to paint watercolours by writing p5.brush sketches Qwen3.5-35B-A3B rewarded by an aesthetic preference model
VLM Navigation Drop a VLM at a random street corner on Earth Scored on kilometres of error
Document OCR & ASR OCR over a million pages in 22 languages and speech recognition over 102 Behind one OpenEnv server; Gemma 4 trained to read and hear Kannada
Port Logistics Re-plan a broken week of container-ship dockings at the Port of Barcelona Graded against a proven optimum; simulates live news, pilots, tugs, and real wind
JetBlue Operations Run JetBlue through a real storm day Two desks talk, then three with the passengers on board
Lean 4 Proofs OpenAI’s Comparator challenges as Harbor tasks Prove a research result in Lean 4, graded by Comparator in a separate sandbox
Math Proofs Write a natural-language proof of an olympiad problem LLM judge grades it 0–7 against the problem’s rubric (QED-Nano recipe)
24 Game Make the target from every card using + − × ÷ Variants include the current year from eight cards and any four-digit number from nine

🚀 Availability

The resource is accessible through the following locations:

  • Source, recipes, and notebooks: Available in the project repository.
  • Environments, datasets, models, and demos: Hosted at huggingface.co/FineEnvs.
  • Training Infrastructure: Supports execution via HF Jobs or Slurm.

#FineEnvs #ReinforcementLearning #OpenSource #LLMTraining #HuggingFace

Source: adithya-s-k/FineEnvs

item.title: Ladybird Browser Releases First Alpha with Rust Migration and Performance Gains
item.description:
Ladybird Browser Releases First Alpha with Rust Migration and Performance Gains

The Ladybird project has released its first alpha version, allowing users on macOS and Linux to install the browser without the need for manual compilation. This project aims to build a new browser by 2026 with its own implementation of core components including HTML parsing, CSS, layout, and JavaScript.

🔍 Overview

Ladybird is a new browser implementation that builds most of its key components internally while utilizing a few established external libraries for specific tasks.

Component External Library
Text shaping HarfBuzz
2D graphics Skia
Video ffmpeg
Database SQLite

🧩 How it works

The browser architecture focuses on isolation and parallel execution to manage web content efficiently.

  • Process Isolation: Ladybird runs different tabs in different processes, an isolation mechanism used by most modern browsers.
  • Threading: The project has moved style and layout tasks to their own dedicated thread.
  • WebAssembly Engine: The browser replaced its C++ WebAssembly engine with Cranelift, achieving a 7x performance boost on the JetStream 3 WASM benchmark.

⚙️ Key details

Significant technical milestones have been reached through AI-assisted development and rigorous testing:

  • Rust Migration: On February 23, 2026, Andreas Kling reported that parts of the LibJS JavaScript engine were ported from C++ to 25,000 lines of Rust in two weeks using Claude Code and Codex.
  • Web Standards Success: The browser gained 75,650 new passes on the web-platform-tests suite, surpassing Safari. The browser now passes approximately 2.18 million subtests.
  • Rapid Development: Most testing gains occurred between October 22 and October 27, 2026. This followed the release of Claude Opus 5.5 on September 22, 2026, and preceded the release of Claude Fable 5.2 on November 9, 2026.
  • Monthly Gains: The project recorded gains of 30,000 in /css and 10,000 in /editing tests within a single month.

🚀 Availability

Pre-compiled binaries for the first alpha are now available for macOS and Linux.

  • Stability: As an alpha software, the browser may crash or fail to load some websites.
  • Reporting: Users can report broken sites from within the browser and have the option to send crash reports after a failure.
  • Security Testing: The developers are inviting security researchers to hack the browser to help harden the system, noting that no security promises are made during this alpha stage.

#Ladybird #Browser #Rust #WebAssembly #OpenSource

item.title: A Curated Survey of Agent Harness Research and Engineering
item.description:
A Curated Survey of Agent Harness Research and Engineering

A curated, multiply-verified survey of agent harness research and engineering — the right level of abstraction for understanding the current frontier of LLM agents.

🔍 Overview

  • Total: 213 papers · 68 production harnesses / essays / talks · last updated 2026-10-26
  • 116 papers + Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / OpenHands tools + Anthropic / OpenAI / Karpathy essays.
  • Agent = Model + Harness.

🧩 How it works

  • The harness is the layer around the model that turns it into an agent — the agent loop plus tools, memory, context, runtime, and safety.
  • You can also define an agent as: agent = model + harness. The harness is the scaffolding around the model that connects it to the real world.
  • This post focuses on the Codex harness, which provides the core agent loop and execution logic that underlies all Codex experiences and is surfaced through the Codex CLI.
  • Agents can handle sophisticated tasks, but their implementation is often straightforward. They are typically just LLMs using tools based on environmental feedback in a loop.
  • The agent loop is therefore a component of the harness — its core execution mechanism — not a peer of it.

⚙️ Key details

Agent / Framework Creator / Org Description Stars / Metrics
Continue Continue Continue — open-source AI coding agent as a VS Code / JetBrains extension, fully local-model friendly. ~34.6k stars
AutoGen Microsoft Research AutoGen — programming framework for building multi-agent conversational systems. ~59.4k stars
Aider Paul Gauthier Aider — AI pair programming in the terminal, git-aware by design. ~47k stars (canonical org: Aider-AI/aider)
OpenHands All-Hands-AI OpenHands (formerly OpenDevin) — open-source platform for autonomous software development with browser, terminal, and co Not specified
SWE-agent Princeton NLP / SWE-agent SWE-agent — agent-computer-interface (ACI) framework that takes a GitHub issue and autonomously fixes it with any LM. ~1
Goose Block (fka Square) Goose — Block’s open-source, extensible AI agent that goes beyond code suggestions to install, execute, edit, and test c Not specified
Cline Cline Cline (formerly Claude Dev) — autonomous coding agent shipped as VS Code extension, SDK, and CLI. ~64k stars
CrewAI CrewAI CrewAI — framework for orchestrating role-playing, collaborative autonomous AI agents (crew, task, tool). ~54.8k stars

#AIagents #MachineLearning #OpenSource #SoftwareDevelopment

item.title: CrowdSec provides open-source IDS/IPS and WAF with community blocklists
item.description:
CrowdSec provides open-source IDS/IPS and WAF with community blocklists

CrowdSec is an open-source, participative security solution that offers crowdsourced server detection and protection against malicious IPs. It operates as an all-in-one IDS/IPS and WAF for Linux, Windows, Docker, and Kubernetes environments, allowing users to detect bad behaviors and actively remediate threats through a shared community blocklist.

🔍 Overview

  • CrowdSec is an open-source security solution that is participative by design.
  • It provides IDS/IPS (Intrusion Detection/Prevention System) and WAF (Web Application Firewall) capabilities.
  • It supports Linux, Windows, Docker, and Kubernetes.
  • It features a crowdsourced blocklist of malicious IPs.
  • Detection rules are available under the MIT license.

🧩 How it works

  • Log Analysis: The Security Engine detects bad behaviors by analyzing log sources and HTTP requests.
  • Decoupled Architecture: Following a “Detect Here, Remedy There” approach, users can parse logs on one machine and block threats at a firewall, reverse proxy, or CDN on another.
  • WAF Capabilities: The AppSec component is built on Coraza, allowing SecLang rules and the OWASP Core Rule Set to load as-is. It also supports a YAML rule format.
  • Bot Mitigation: AppSec can answer suspicious requests with a JavaScript proof-of-work challenge at tunable difficulty, stopping headless browsers and scrapers while allowing verified crawlers like Googlebot to pass.
  • Community Blocklist: An IP identified as malicious by one user is added to a curated list, proactively blocking that IP for all other users before it reaches their systems.

⚙️ Key details

  • Scenarios: Ships by default with scenarios for brute force, port scan, and web scan.
  • Customization: Users can extend protection by picking more scenarios from the Hub or creating their own.
  • Remediation: Allows active remediation using Remediation Components.
  • Comparison: Unlike fail2ban, CrowdSec decouples detection and remediation; unlike ModSecurity or naxsi, it shares IP reputation and remediation layers with the log-based engine.

🚀 Availability

  • Installation is available for Linux, Windows, Docker, OpnSense, and Kubernetes.
  • The Community Blocklist is available in real-time.
  • Detection rules are hosted on the CrowdSec Hub.

#CrowdSec #Cybersecurity #IDS #WAF #OpenSource #BotDetection

Source: crowdsecurity/crowdsec

item.title: AnythingMCP Launched as an Open-Source Gateway for AI Model Connectivity
item.description:
AnythingMCP Launched as an Open-Source Gateway for AI Model Connectivity

AnythingMCP is a newly released open-source, self-hosted Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway designed to connect AI clients like Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini to enterprise software and internal documents without the need for developers to write custom MCP servers.

🧩 Core Architecture and Features

AnythingMCP functions as a central layer that stores enterprise data in a unified “knowledge graph of how your systems connect,” alongside AI skills and company memory. This data is shared across all connected AI clients while respecting individual user roles.

Key Technical Capabilities

  • Extensive Connectivity: Offers 957 ready connectors supporting over 12,000 tools, including integrations with SAP, Odoo, weclapp, and Amazon Seller. 51 of these connectors operate without an API key.
  • Custom Protocol Support: Provides 696 catalog connectors or supports custom REST, OpenAPI, SOAP, GraphQL, OData, SQL, IMAP, SMTP, and MCP sources. Tools register at runtime.
  • Document Indexing: Indexes SFTP, FTP/FTPS, WebDAV (Nextcloud, NAS), S3, and network shares. It extracts data from PDF pages, Excel rows (including column names), Word documents, PowerPoint files, and Outlook emails with attachments.
  • Traceability: AI answers are returned with specific file, page, and date references for verification.
  • File Management: Generates temporary download links for user files and AI-generated files (such as CSV exports or reports), supporting both internal and public access with expiration and revocation capabilities.
  • Cross-Client Memory: Facts and preferences saved in one AI client are accessible in others (e.g., data entered in Claude is usable by Copilot). Memory is managed with personal and company scopes, organized by folders and role limits.
  • Agent Procedures: Supports procedures that AI agents follow, which can be written manually or learned from actual requests.

⚙️ Usage Example

The gateway enables complex queries spanning multiple systems, such as asking a single question in Claude that is answered using data from Etsy, SAP, and a logistics API simultaneously.

🚀 Availability and Usage

  • Cloud Presence: AnythingMCP Cloud hosts over 16,000 workspaces and processes more than 1.5 million AI tool calls per month.
  • Listing Status: The service is listed in the official Claude directory and the ChatGPT Plugin Directory.
  • Trial Access: A free 7-day trial of the Cloud service is available.

#MCP #AIIntegration #EnterpriseAI #OpenSource #Claude #ChatGPT

item.title: DeepSeek AI releases open-source agent harness in developer preview
item.description:
DeepSeek AI releases open-source agent harness in developer preview

DeepSeek AI has released DeepSeek Harness (dsh), an open-source agent harness that is currently in developer preview.

🧩 How it works

DeepSeek Harness is built on an everything-is-a-plugin architecture. The system is powered by Cordis, a design described in the paper A Programming Paradigm for Spatiotemporal Composability.

⚙️ Key details

The project is iterating rapidly and will introduce compatibility-breaking changes. Users are advised to review the safety notice before running the project. Third-party dependencies and their licenses are disclosed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

To run the tool from a repository checkout, the following steps are required:

  • git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git
  • cd deepseek-harness
  • pnpm install
  • pnpm run build
  • pnpm dsh web

Running pnpm run build prepares the repository artifacts, while pnpm dsh web uses those built artifacts without rebuilding. For local development, pnpm run dev:web builds, serves, and rebuilds client bundles on source edits in a single terminal.

🚀 Availability

DeepSeek Harness is currently in developer preview.

  • Quick Start: Install Node.js, then run npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web.
  • Web UI: The command starts the Web UI at http://127.0.0.1:3080 by default and opens it in the default browser.
  • SSH Launch: Only the host URL is printed because the SSH client or editor owns the local forwarded address.
  • No Browser: Pass --no-open to run the server without opening a browser.

Feedback and bug reports can be submitted through GitHub Discussions. For plugin discoverability, developers should add the dsh-plugin topic to their repositories.

#DeepSeek #AIagents #OpenSource #DeveloperPreview #Cordis

Source: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness

Researchers have released HUGE-Bench, an open-source UAV simulation platform targeting high-level vision-language-action tasks where agents ground brief, potentially ambiguous commands into safe, multi-stage behaviors. item.title: Limut – Browser‑Based Live‑Coding for Music and Visuals
item.description:
Limut – Browser‑Based Live‑Coding for Music and Visuals

Limut is a new browser‑based live‑coding environment for music and visuals, built to be instantly accessible without any installation.

🔍 Overview

  • Live coding of music and visuals runs directly in any modern browser.
  • Inspired by FoxDot’s approach to live‑coding music, with the goal of requiring no install.
  • Visual rendering draws inspiration from Crash Server’s video player and the Shadertoy community.

🧩 How it works

  • The interface uses the CodeMirror editor, which provides syntax coloring for Limut code.
  • Documentation lives on the same page, positioned beneath the console.
  • Example code snippets are embedded on the page; additional examples and technical tests are available in the repository at examples.limut.
  • Unit tests execute automatically when the page is loaded with the ?test URL parameter; results appear in the browser console.
  • The Shadertoy synth loads shader code directly from the Shadertoy.com API, reusing many community shaders.

⚙️ Key details

  • Audio sources: piano samples from the Salamander Grand Piano V3 (CC BY 3.0), guitar samples from FreePats FSBS Electric Guitar Direct (CC0 1.0), guitar release/muted noises from Karoryfer Shinyguitar (CC0 1.0). Additional waveform tables come from GoogleChromeLabs’ Web Audio Samples (Apache) and include Adventure Kid WaveForms and WaveEdit Online tables.
  • Compatibility: Normal development maintains backward compatibility; occasional breaking changes trigger a new GitHub release that documents the upgrade path.
  • Testing: Adding ?test to the URL runs the built‑in unit tests; output is shown in the console.
  • Packaging: Limut can be served as a static website or wrapped as a desktop app using Electron (npm install then npm start). No pre‑packaged binaries are provided yet; contributions are welcome via pull requests.

🚀 Availability

  • Live demo: https://sdclibbery.github.io/limut/
  • Source code and examples: https://github.com/sdclibbery/limut/blob/master/examples.limut
  • Issue tracker: https://github.com/sdclibbery/limut/issues
  • Release notes: https://github.com/sdclibbery/limut/releases
  • Local development: run ./server.sh and open http://localhost:8000/?test in a browser.

💡 Why it matters

  • Removes the installation barrier for live‑coding music and visual performances.
  • Leverages existing open‑source audio and shader assets, keeping the project lightweight and extensible.
  • Provides a single, browser‑native environment that combines code editing, documentation, and testing in one page.

item.title: LLM-Assisted Hardware Hacking Enables Custom Firmware and Interface Redesigns for Consumer Devices
item.description:
LLM-Assisted Hardware Hacking Enables Custom Firmware and Interface Redesigns for Consumer Devices

Large language models are being used to redesign and upgrade hardware devices through a process known as vibe hacking. By prompting tools like Claude Code or Codex, users are modifying various consumer electronics including televisions, digital cameras, synthesizers, and gaming consoles. This development has created a new market for custom software and led to a surge in developer-friendly gadgets.

🔍 Overview

  • Large language models (LLMs) can find hidden APIs and unpack firmware files located on websites.
  • Users can repackage hardware software to add new capabilities or redesign user interfaces.
  • This trend has empowered both professional developers and non-developers to build custom software for their own devices.
  • While many modifications target Android-based systems, hardware such as dishwashers and luxury cars often run similar underlying software that remains susceptible to these methods.

🧩 How it works

To modify hardware using an LLM, users typically follow a technical process involving specific permissions and debugging tools. For example, a developer in India named Gathin T used Claude Code to modify a Xiaomi Android TV by enabling USB debugging and applying permissions tweaks. Once established on the same Wi-Fi network, the chatbot can explore, unpack, and repackage firmware to the user’s liking.

⚙️ Key details

Device Category Example Hardware Modification Details
Televisions Android-based (Xiaomi) Redesigned interfaces, removed ads, and simplified input switching via CleanYourTV
Cameras Various Digital Cameras Added recording capabilities, higher resolutions, and new color profiles
Musical Gear M‑Vave FM‑1 Installed custom open-source firmware and new features on cheap synthesizers
Game Consoles PlayStation 5 Created scripts for cross-device controller use and enabled PlayStation 2 disc playback

🚀 Availability

The ability to hack hardware using LLMs saw a significant increase in late 2025 when Claude Code reached a functional milestone. Throughout 2026, the practice expanded as more people pointed these capabilities at their big screens and handheld devices. Notable repositories like CleanYourTV have appeared on GitHub, receiving thousands of pull requests and feature ideas from the community.

💡 Why it matters

This shift toward AI-assisted hardware modification is changing how manufacturers approach security and intellectual property. Luke Dicken, a gaming executive and former head of artificial intelligence at Take‑Two, predicted that the industry may respond with more invasive DRM, platform-level solutions, and a push toward streaming to prevent decompilation. Additionally, users who install vibe-coded firmware operate outside official support channels and may face technical issues that the manufacturer is not equipped to solve.

#ClaudeCode #HardwareHacking #Firmware #VibeCoding #OpenSource

Source: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets

item.title: OpenNHP toolkit hides infrastructure using zero-trust cryptography
item.description:
OpenNHP toolkit hides infrastructure using zero-trust cryptography

OpenNHP is a lightweight, cryptography-powered, open-source toolkit implementing Zero Trust security for infrastructure, applications, and data. It serves as the reference implementation of the Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) Network-infrastructure Hiding Protocol (NHP) specification.

🔍 Overview

OpenNHP is designed to hide servers, ports, and domains from the public internet. In the AI era, visibility equates to vulnerability; OpenNHP inverts this model by remaining invisible until trusted. Consequently, scanners, bots, and AI-driven attackers find nothing to attack because nothing answers until a client proves its identity with a single encrypted packet.

🧩 How it works

The toolkit features two core protocols and a modular design inspired by the NIST Zero Trust Architecture:

  • Network-infrastructure Hiding Protocol (NHP): Conceals server ports, IP addresses, and domain names to protect applications and infrastructure from unauthorized access.
  • Data-content Hiding Protocol (DHP): Ensures data security and privacy via encryption and confidential computing, making data “usable but not visible.”

The architecture includes specific components that slot alongside existing IAM, DNS, FIDO, and Zero Trust policy engines:

Component Function
NHP-Agent Client that sends encrypted knock requests to gain access
NHP-Server Authenticates and authorizes requests; runs separately and is architecturally decoupled from the protected host
NHP-AC Access controller that manages firewall rules on the protected server
NHP-Relay HTTP-to-UDP bridge enabling browser-based agents to send NHP knocks via HTTPS
NHP-KGC Key Generation Center for Identity-Based Cryptography (IBC)

The workflow operates on a default-deny gate for every port, IP, and hostname:

  1. Registration (once per device): The agent generates its own key pair and enrolls the public key. The agent requests a one-time password (NHP_OTP), which the Server’s auth plugin delivers to the user (e.g., by email). The agent sends the OTP and its public key (NHP_REG), and the Server binds the key to the user and replies (NHP_RAK). The private key never leaves the device.
  2. Knock (every access): The agent sends an encrypted knock (NHP_KNK) to the Server. The Server validates the knock and sends an operation.

💡 Why it matters

Attackers can’t exploit what they can’t discover. NHP represents a next step in “hide the service first” designs, extending security stacks rather than forking them.

#OpenNHP #ZeroTrust #Cybersecurity #InfrastructureSecurity #OpenSource

Source: OpenNHP/opennhp

item.title: SocratiCode Releases Open-Source Codebase Context Engine for AI Assistants
item.description:
SocratiCode Releases Open-Source Codebase Context Engine for AI Assistants

SocratiCode has launched as an open-source, zero-configuration codebase context engine designed to give AI assistants automated, deep semantic understanding of entire codebases and infrastructure. Operating locally and privately by default, the platform enables development teams to index, analyze, and query massive codebases without sending data outside their machines.

🔍 Overview

SocratiCode provides a private-by-default context engine that runs via Docker, requiring no API keys. It allows AI assistants to understand codebases of up to and over 40 million lines of code with zero setup, supporting Model Context Protocol (MCP) hosts via local stdio servers, as well as plugins and extensions.

⚙️ Key Features

  • High Efficiency: Delivers deep codebase intelligence while being 37x faster, using 61% fewer tokens, and requiring 84% fewer calls.
  • Deep Code Intelligence: Provides hybrid semantic search, cross-project and branch-aware search, polyglot dependency graphs, symbol-level impact analysis, and an interactive HTML graph explorer.
  • Broad Knowledge Base: Indexes databases, API specs, infrastructure configurations, and architecture docs as searchable context artifacts.
  • Automated Management: Features batched, resumable indexing that saves progress during interruptions, and an automatic file watcher that tracks changes across sessions.
  • Multi-Agent Coordination: Supports multiple AI agents working on the same codebase simultaneously, sharing a single index with zero configuration.

🛡️ Ecosystem and Governance

Developers who need security policies and governance alongside codebase context can integrate with SocratiCode’s sibling project:

Project Description
JanuScope A local-first MCP policy proxy providing tool blocking, SQL-mutation gating, PII redaction, auditing, and rate-limiting.

🚀 Availability

  • SocratiCode Open-Source: The core engine is open-source, fully private, and remains free forever.
  • SocratiCode Cloud (Private Beta): A hosted option featuring a shared team index, SSO, audit logs, branch-aware indexing, and VPC or air-gapped deployment options is currently in private beta.

#SocratiCode #OpenSource #DeveloperTools #AIagents #ModelContextProtocol

item.description:
Omnilogue Open-Source Tool for Offline Browsing of AI Coding Assistant History

Omnilogue is an open‑source desktop application with an optional self‑hosted WebUI that lets you browse, search, and analyze the history of many AI coding assistants while keeping all data local.

🔍 Overview

  • Desktop app and web server to browse, search and analyze AI coding assistant history — Claude Code, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, Cursor, OpenCode and more.
  • 100 % offline; the app reads conversation files on disk and does not upload session data or require an Omnilogue account.
  • Supports a long list of assistants, including Aider, Amazon Q CLI, Antigravity, Claude Code, Cline, CodeBuddy, Codex CLI, Continue.dev, Cursor, ForgeCode, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, OpenHands, PearAI, Pi, Qoder, Qwen Code, Zed, and many others.

🧩 How it works

  • The desktop app reads local conversation files; an optional server can be run on the same machine for browser access.
  • Example server binds to loopback only and is reachable at http://127.0.0.1:3727.
  • Server guide covers prebuilt binaries, Docker, and authentication for network access.
  • Technical requirements: Node.js 20.19+ (or 22.12+), pnpm, and a stable Rust toolchain. Linux build prerequisites are listed in the Linux guide.
  • Build the desktop bundle with pnpm tauri:build.

⚙️ Key details

  • Platforms: macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows x64, Linux x86‑64.
  • Installation: desktop download for each platform; macOS Homebrew support; Flatpak and other Linux packages via the Linux guide.
  • Updates: existing installs can update in place while keeping favorites and settings.
  • Usage insights: review tokens and estimated API costs where logs provide data; separate visibility into sub‑agent work.
  • Session navigation: find conversations again, browse by project or assistant, search across sessions, follow conversation branches, jump between steps, and inspect tool calls and file edits.

🚀 Availability

  • Download links are provided for each supported OS.
  • macOS users may also install via Homebrew.
  • Linux users can use Flatpak or follow the Linux guide for other package managers.
  • The optional WebUI server can be run locally; see the server guide for details.

💡 Why it matters

  • Keeps AI coding assistant history fully local, protecting privacy and avoiding external accounts.
