item.title: Amazon Upgrades Bedrock AgentCore with Strands Harness and Gateway Interceptors
item.description:
Amazon Upgrades Bedrock AgentCore with Strands Harness and Gateway Interceptors

Amazon is upgrading the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness to use Strands harness, an open-source agent harness released under an Apache 2.0 license. This update introduces lifecycle hooks, automatic prompt caching, and proactive context management alongside new security features for enterprise-grade tool execution and data protection.

🔍 Overview

With this upgrade, the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness operates on top of Strands harness, which acts as an assembled agent foundation with recommended instructions, tools, and context management. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runs this foundation as a managed AWS service, eliminating the need to provision compute, bundle and host the agent loop, manage session scaling, or operate tool-execution infrastructure.

🧩 How it works

Each agent session runs in a secure, kernel-isolated microVM in the AgentCore runtime, which connects the harness to the production services required by enterprise agents:

  • Session Execution: Handled automatically with managed compute, scaling, and high availability.
  • Integration Services: Connects directly to session persistence, streaming responses, usage metadata, observability, AgentCore memory, Identity, and Gateway.
  • Control Balance: Developers retain control over instructions, tools, models, permissions, and lifecycle policies while AgentCore manages the underlying execution environment.

⚙️ Key details

The upgrade introduces a suite of native features designed to reduce latency, cost, and complexity:

  • Lifecycle Hooks: Allows developers to apply custom deterministic checks and notifications at defined points in the agent loop.
  • Prompt Caching: For supported Converse models, the harness caches system prompts, tool definitions, and conversation history to reduce latency and input token costs.
  • Context Optimization: Summarizes older conversation turns once the context window reaches a configurable threshold, running at about 34% lower token cost than other leading harnesses.

Built-In Tools

The upgrade brings several new built-in capabilities for managing agent workflows:

Tool Name Functionality
todo_write Maintains a structured task plan that can be restored in later sessions, even after context summarization.
subagent Delegates self-contained tasks to fresh worker agents and returns results to the parent.
web_fetch Retrieves content from specified webpages to provide up-to-date external context.
Filesystem Access Granular read, write, and edit tools to control the filesystem capabilities granted to agents.

💡 Why it matters

As agents interact with third-party tools, SaaS APIs, and web search engines, sensitive data (such as names, account numbers, or card details) can leave the AWS account and compliance scope through tool arguments. To address this, AgentCore Gateway fronts every tool an agent uses and supports request and response interceptors via AWS Lambda.

By adding Skyflow Detect to AgentCore Gateway as an interceptor, sensitive entities are detected and replaced with reversible vault tokens before data reaches tools, and restored before the agent reads the tool’s results.

This configuration enables three protection modes:

  • Shield the tool: Strips sensitive values from arguments on the way out and restores them in results on the way back, protecting third-party APIs from receiving customer identities.
  • Shield the model: De-identifies prompts, history, files, and tool results before the model reads them.
  • Shield the document: Replaces original document links from tools with clean copies before the agent opens them.

For example, a large European bank uses these tools to investigate card disputes. When an agent searches the web for a merchant, the Skyflow interceptor replaces the customer’s name with a reversible token (e.g. [NAME_AJbrIud]). The search provider receives a safe query, while the authorized analyst still sees the correct customer details in the agent’s final response.

🚀 Availability

  • Strands Harness: Open-source under the Apache 2.0 license.
  • Skyflow Detect Interceptor: Open source on GitHub.
  • Skyflow Vault: Available on the AWS Marketplace.

#AmazonBedrock #AIagents #AWS #OpenSource #DataSecurity

Source: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness adds Strands harness defaults, built-in tools, and lifecycle hooks | Amazon Web Services Source: Protect agent tool calls with Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Community fork enables local execution of Japanese Government AI GenAI
item.description:
Community fork enables local execution of Japanese Government AI GenAI

A community-driven project has forked the Japanese Digital Agency’s open-source Government AI “GenAI” (Genai) to enable full local operation using local Large Language Models (LLMs) with an OpenAI-compatible API. This unofficial fork addresses the original system’s dependency on cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) by replacing those dependencies with local or open-source alternatives, allowing the software to run in closed network environments such as LGWAN.

🧩 How it works

The project modifies the Digital Agency’s genai-web repository (MIT License) to function in a local environment. To facilitate merging with upstream changes, the majority of modifications are concentrated in the OpenGENAI layer (backend/ and external apps), while the genai-web UI is kept largely unmodified to preserve the original user experience. The original genai-ai-api is not included in the fork; users must obtain it separately from the Digital Agency’s repository if needed.

⚙️ Key details

The fork currently stands at version v0.13.0. Key technical and functional features include:

  • Hardware Flexibility: Compatible with macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux systems with NVIDIA GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA DGX Spark).
  • Security & Deployment: Production builds use docker-compose.prod.yml with TLS termination on port 443. Closed-network verification uses docker-compose.verify.yml with HTTP on port 80.
  • Storage: Uses SeaweedFS (port 8333), which is not exposed to the host in production. Artifact downloads are handled via a reverse proxy through S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT.
  • Core Capabilities: Includes structured RAG, MCP integration, OCR, skills, Web SSH, and PII detection.

📋 Version History

Version Key Developments
v0.13.0 Training, procedure document/audit, and scheduling wizard
v0.12.0 Two-week work, draw.io editing, image generation chat, and per-building model control
v0.11.0 Multi-tenancy, recommended apps, and Markdown editor HTML/PPTX export
v0.10.0 Notebook features (research/organization), Web SSH, and app display editing
v0.9.0 Third implementation wave: Markdown editor and document creation with pluggable generation APIs
v0.8.0 Second implementation wave: Online forms, procedure bundles, application reception, and MCP
v0.7.0 First implementation wave: Document reading/checking, scheduling, and Excel generation
v0.6.0 PII detection, knowledge base pages, large attachment mapreduce, and Dify error classification
v0.5.0 Production static build deployment, multi-model swapping, and SAML authentication hardening
v0.4.0 Structured RAG, knowledge MCP, Dify integration examples, and My Number checking

💡 Why it matters

The project is explicitly an unofficial fork with no relationship to or approval from the Digital Agency. While early releases focused on replacing cloud dependencies with local/OSS components, the project’s philosophy has expanded to support actual municipal usage in closed networks. This allows local governments and organizations to utilize GenAI capabilities for administrative tasks (such as document processing and scheduling) without relying on external cloud services.

item.title: Microsoft publishes open-source Model Context Protocol curriculum and Qdrant memory server
item.description:
Microsoft publishes open-source Model Context Protocol curriculum and Qdrant memory server

Microsoft has released an open-source curriculum for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) alongside an official MCP server for Qdrant, enabling developers to build modular, secure AI workflows and implement semantic memory layers using specific language examples and vector search integration.

🧩 The MCP Curriculum

The new open-source curriculum introduces the fundamentals of MCP through real-world, cross-language examples. It is designed for developers to learn practical techniques for building modular, scalable, and secure AI workflows, covering everything from session setup to service orchestration.

  • Languages Covered: C#, Java, JavaScript, Rust, Python, and TypeScript.
  • Repository: The resources are hosted at https://github.com/microsoft/mcp-for-beginners.git.
  • Global Accessibility: The repository includes more than 50 language translations. Note that these translations significantly increase the download size.
  • Community Support: Developers can join the Microsoft Foundry Discord community using the provided link.

🧠 The Qdrant MCP Server

The release includes an official Model Context Protocol server for keeping and retrieving memories in the Qdrant vector search engine. This server acts as a semantic memory layer on top of the Qdrant database and is based on FastMCP.

Core Tools

  • qdrant-store: Stores information in the Qdrant database.
  • qdrant-find: Retrieves relevant information from the Qdrant database.

Configuration Details

Configuration is handled via environment variables, and the only command-line argument is --transport, which selects the transport protocol. You cannot provide both QDRANT_URL and QDRANT_LOCAL_PATH simultaneously.

Environment Variable Description
QDRANT_LOCAL_PATH Path to the local Qdrant database (alternative to QDRANT_URL)
EMBEDDING_PROVIDER Embedding provider to use (currently only “fastembed” is supported)
EMBEDDING_MODEL Name of the embedding model to use
QDRANT_SEARCH_LIMIT Maximum number of results to return from search
QDRANT_READ_ONLY Enable read-only mode (disables qdrant-store tool)
FASTMCP_HOST Host address to bind the server to (SSE and HTTP transports)
FASTMCP_PORT Port to run the server on (SSE and HTTP transports)
FASTMCP_MASK_ERROR_DETAILS Hide exception details from tool error messages sent to clients

Naming Conventions

Before version 0.9.0, settings used the FASTMCP_SERVER_ prefix (e.g., FASTMCP_SERVER_HOST). The old names FASTMCP_SERVER_HOST, FASTMCP_SERVER_PORT, and FASTMCP_SERVER_DEBUG still work but are deprecated and will be removed in a future release. If both old and new names are set, the new name takes precedence.

🚀 Availability and Usage

The mcp-server-qdrant can be run directly without specific installation steps by using uvx. The server supports different transport protocols specified using the --transport flag.

#MCP #Microsoft #Qdrant #AIDevelopment #OpenSource

Source: microsoft/mcp-for-beginners Source: qdrant/mcp-server-qdrant

item.title: PenShot multi-agent system converts scripts to video generation prompts
item.description:
PenShot multi-agent system converts scripts to video generation prompts

A new open-source system called PenShot uses a multi-agent LangGraph pipeline to parse scripts of any format and generate coherent, model-ready prompts for text-to-video models including Sora, Veo, Runway, Kling, and SVD.

🔍 Overview

PenShot (剧本分镜智能体) is a script-to-storyboard agent that takes input from movies, anime, short dramas, or novels and produces shot-level descriptions and video generation prompts. It is built on LLMs orchestrated through LangGraph and LlamaIndex, with a focus on maintaining character, scene, and plot consistency across segments.

🧩 How it works

The system operates as a directed multi-agent graph:

  • Script parsing agent → Storyboard generation agent
  • Storyboard generation agent → Video segmentation agent
  • Video segmentation agent → Prompt conversion agent
  • Prompt conversion agent → Quality audit agent
  • Quality audit agent → Continuity guard agent
  • Continuity guard agent → Auxiliary generation agent (three-view/background/keyframe)
  • Multi-model adapter → Sora / Veo / Runway / 可灵 / SVD
  • Sora / Veo / Runway / 可灵 / SVD → FFmpeg synthesis
  • FFmpeg synthesis → Final film

Continuity is enforced through a three-view design, a RAG knowledge base, three-tier memory (short/medium/long term), Chroma vector retrieval, snapshot mechanism, and multi-dimensional recall. A task-pool priority queue manages execution order.

⚙️ Key details

Supported input and output

  • Accepts arbitrary-format scripts: movies, short dramas, anime, novels
  • Auto-identifies scenes, dialogue, and action instructions
  • Understands story structure and supports long-text segmented processing
  • Outputs shot-granularity segments with precise duration planning adapted to each video model’s length limits

Prompt generation

  • Bilingual (Chinese/English) visual descriptions
  • Negative prompts
  • Audio prompts
  • Ready-to-use for Sora, Veo, Runway, Kling (可灵), SVD

Model and LLM compatibility

Component Options
Text-to-video models Sora, Veo, Runway, 可灵, SVD
LLM providers OpenAI, Qwen, DeepSeek, Ollama (pluggable)

Integration interfaces

  • Python SDK
  • REST API
  • LangGraph nodes
  • Function Calling
  • MCP (Model Context Protocol) standard interface
  • A2A collaboration protocol

Reliability features

  • Automatic retry and error fallback
  • Bidirectional traceability: every storyboard segment links back to its source script position

🚀 Availability

  • Package install: pip install penshot (3 lines of code to integrate)
  • Docker: docker pull neotems/penshot to run as a service
  • Claimed 5-minute onboarding

💡 Why it matters

PenShot addresses the gap between narrative scripts and the strict prompt requirements of current text-to-video models. By combining multi-agent orchestration, persistent memory, vector retrieval, and multi-model adapter layers, it provides an end-to-end pipeline that preserves narrative continuity while outputting prompts tailored to each target video generator.

#AIagents #LangGraph #TextToVideo #ScriptToVideo #MultiAgent #OpenSource

Source: neopen/story-shot-agent

item.title: SME Memory Engine Adds Spatial Regions and Explainable Retrieval
item.description:
SME Memory Engine Adds Spatial Regions and Explainable Retrieval

A new long-term memory engine for AI applications called SME has been released, featuring self-organizing spatial memory regions, Ebbinghaus-inspired memory dynamics, and an explainable eight-signal retrieval system. The system runs offline with zero configuration and works with any OpenAI-compatible LLM or embedding model, whether cloud or local.

🔍 Overview

SME organizes all memories into a continuous embedding space where writes automatically form density-driven Memory Regions that dynamically grow, split, and merge. Regions connect via graph links. Memories also maintain six semantic edge types forming a Memory Graph: reference, causal, dialogue, summary, parent-child, and neighbor. Memory dynamics layer Ebbinghaus reinforcement, time decay (without deletion), automatic merging, and long-term compression on top.

🧩 How It Works

Two-stage hybrid retrieval combines region-led recall with vector/BM25 (Chinese bigram)/metadata hybrid search, optional graph enhancement, and an eight-signal explainable ranking. The 1.3 retrieval update adds min-max hybrid fusion (measured at +2.5 to +4.2 percentage points accuracy across three seed A/B tests, with bias halved) and Personalized PageRank graph expansion following the HippoRAG 2 approach to surface bridging associations. Optional idle-time automatic reorganization (sleep-time compute) and ONNX int8 embeddings are available via the [onnx] extra.

Memory lifecycle includes configurable reinforcement, decay, merging, and compression. Memories are never deleted due to decay and can be restored from archive.

⚙️ Key Details

Extension Modules (12 total, all disabled by default for base behavior)

Module Function
Fact extraction Extracts structured facts from input
QA pair replay Replays question-answer pairs
Temporal knowledge graph Builds time-aware knowledge graphs
User profiling Maintains user profiles
Fact version correction Corrects fact versions over time
Noise suppression Filters noisy inputs
WAL incremental persistence Write-ahead log for durability
Storage backend Pluggable storage
REST + SDK API and Python SDK access
Observability Metrics and monitoring
Hierarchical context Multi-level context management
Multi-user isolation Isolates memory per user

Presets (7 configurations)

  • Chat assistant
  • Knowledge base dynamic
  • Knowledge base static
  • Embodied robot
  • All off
  • Static retrieval · UNITED
  • Real model · semantic priority

Interfaces

  • Python SDK
  • REST API (FastAPI) with official client
  • MCP (agent-native, one-line mount)
  • Web configuration center (python -m sme.api then open browser)

Chinese-Friendly Features

  • Chinese 1-2 gram BM25 keyword channel enabled by default
  • Document clause import for legal/medical knowledge base scenarios

Explainable Retrieval

Every hit includes a breakdown of eight signals: semantic, importance, freshness, weight, decay, hit_count, recency, and region.

🚀 Availability

Installation: Zero-config offline operation. After installing core dependencies, a built-in hashing embedding runs the basic pipeline with no model downloads or API keys.

Core dependencies: numpy, httpx, fastapi, uvicorn, networkx, python-multipart, hnswlib (in [ann] extra). Install via pip install -r requirements.txt or pip install -e . (with pip install -e ".[ann]" for ANN acceleration; region scaling automatically enables ANN, falling back to exact scan otherwise).

Requirements: Python ≥ 3.10, Windows or Linux.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Benchmarked head-to-head against Mem0 and bare RAG
  • All 101 configuration items and 7 presets are fully toggleable
  • Performance figures: WAL group commit 2,557 writes/sec (1.79×), ONNX int8 batch embedding 7.4×, memory graph hot path O(E)→O(deg) measured 127–159×, hashing retrieval p50 ~4 ms at 2k items
  • Runs entirely offline with zero external dependencies for the base path

#AIMemory #RAG #LLM #Embeddings #OpenSource

Source: jack66g/spatial-memory-engine

item.title: Solar framework launches open tools for real-time video world models
item.description:
Solar framework launches open tools for real-time video world models

Solar is an open framework for interactive world models that spans open data, scalable training, long-horizon video generation, and real-time deployment. The repository contains code for two primary components: SolarWM and SolarRenderer.

🧩 How it works

The framework is built around two distinct modules that handle different aspects of video generation and rendering:

Component Function
SolarWM Enables real-time interaction, continuous exploration, and diverse generated worlds.
SolarRenderer Performs four-step, structure-conditioned video rendering with bidirectional and block-causal training and inference on MiniMax-H3.

⚙️ Key details

Several specific model releases and optimizations are included in the Solar framework:

  • SolarWM-H3 Memory: Improves long-term scene consistency and preserves visual details across revisits. Weights are available for the 33B model.
  • SolarWM-H3 Realtime: Enables low-latency interactive video generation from an image and a prompt, featuring real-time camera control.
  • H3 Streaming VAE Decoder: Allows for low-latency streaming video decoding that produces frames as latents arrive. It supports both the official MiniMax-H3 VAE and NVIDIA’s distilled StreamRender-H3 decoder.
  • Training Efficiency: Training for SolarWM-H3 is speeded up by 1.9–2.1× across Stage0.5, Stage1, and Stage2 with matching training trajectories, attributed to ResearchBoost-Agent.
  • Data: The SolarWM dataset and SolarRenderer dataset are hosted on Hugging Face.

🚀 Availability

  • Code: SolarWM and SolarRenderer code is available in the repository. Real-time deployment for SolarWM and the H3 Streaming VAE Decoder code are located in the deploy/solar_wm/ directory.
  • Weights: Model weights for both SolarWM and SolarRenderer are available on Hugging Face.
  • Demonstrations: An online demo for SolarRenderer is available on Hugging Face Spaces.
  • Documentation: Specific documentation for SolarWM is found in docs/solar_wm/ and for SolarRenderer in docs/solar_renderer/.

#SolarFramework #VideoGeneration #WorldModels #OpenSource #MiniMax-H3

item.title: RadixArk Releases DaisyRose-27B Model With RL Training on Long-Horizon Agent Tasks
item.description:
RadixArk Releases DaisyRose-27B Model With RL Training on Long-Horizon Agent Tasks

RadixArk has released DaisyRose-27B, its first model, built on Qwen3.8-27B and trained with reinforcement learning using the Miles framework. The model was trained on 1,200 curated long-horizon agent tasks over 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs, achieving a Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 improvement from 5.6% to 12.0%.

🔍 Overview

  • First model release from RadixArk
  • Base: Qwen3.8-27B
  • Training method: Reinforcement learning via Miles (open-source RL framework)
  • Training scale: 1,200 tasks, sessions up to 1M tokens, 18 days, 144 H200 GPUs
  • License: Apache 2.0 checkpoints available

🧩 How It Works

Task Design

  • Tasks built in partnership with Eigent AI from a large pool covering machine learning, software engineering, science, and other fields
  • Thousands of candidates filtered to ~1,200 final tasks using three criteria:
    • Each task targets a mistake the original Qwen3.8-27B makes
    • Tasks redesigned around those mistakes, difficulty adjusted until solve rate falls in a useful learning range
    • Each task requires several interdependent steps: the agent must reason, plan, and execute across a long job
  • Each attempt runs up to 1.5 hours in a sandbox with >100 tool calls and >256K output tokens
  • Tasks must reward actually solving the problem; every task reviewed alongside model attempts; flawed tasks fixed or removed

Training Backend (Miles)

  • Fully asynchronous mode: agent keeps working while model learns, neither waits for the other
  • 128 H200s run inference on agent tasks; 16 H200s run the trainer
  • After each step, updated model deployed to the 128 inference GPUs
  • Internal training backend built for agent training: each step learns from a handful of very long sessions (up to 1M tokens) folded into multiple trajectories via harness summarization

Sandbox Service

  • Built on open-source AgentENV project (RadixArk contributes fixes)
  • Mid-September to mid-November: ~944,000 sandboxes run, up to 1,566 concurrent
  • Service scaled from 1 to 12 machines
  • 10 upgrades shipped, nearly all while training was running
  • 99% sandbox creation success across 9 weeks; >99.95% since late October

⚙️ Key Details

Benchmark Results

Benchmark Qwen3.8-27B DaisyRose-27B
Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 5.6% 12.0%
  • DaisyRose-27B scores higher than original Qwen3.8-27B on every benchmark evaluated
  • Largest gain on Terminal-Bench 4.1 (5.6% → 12.0%)
  • Gains also on reasoning, instruction following, and coding benchmarks
  • Scores use higher of BF16 and FP8 runs; difference <1 point where both evaluated

Model Architecture

  • Retains Qwen3.8-27B architecture, tokenizer, chat template, image understanding, and 256K-token context window
  • Longer training sessions use harness summarization to span multiple trajectories
  • Model thinks before answering by default; reasoning returned in reasoning_content, final answer in content

Training Efficiency

Metric RadixArk Backend Open-Source Trainer (Megatron)
Model FLOPs Utilization (MFU) 37% 16%
Training cost reduction 57% less GPU time baseline
Throughput (tokens/sec across 144 GPUs) ~16,800 ~8,300
End-to-end speed 2× faster baseline
  • Stability: 63,000 GPU-hours over weeks; speed and efficiency held steady from first to last step
  • Larger gains on mixture-of-experts models: 6.2× on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, >10× on ~300B GLM-5.3-Flash

🚀 Availability

  • Checkpoints released under Apache 2.0
  • Recommended serving: SGLang with DSpark speculative decoding
  • SGLang cookbook provides launch configurations for different GPUs and checkpoint formats
  • Quickstart: start server with served model name DaisyRose-27B on port 30000, then send requests via OpenAI Python client

💡 Why It Matters

  • Demonstrates that carefully designed long-horizon agent tasks, an efficient asynchronous RL backend, and a robust sandbox service can jointly deliver large benchmark gains with substantially lower compute cost
  • 57% less GPU time for equivalent training via higher MFU (37% vs 16%)
  • 2× end-to-end throughput improvement
  • Sandbox infrastructure proved reliable at scale (99.95% success rate) with live upgrades during training
  • Gains generalize across benchmark categories and are especially pronounced on mixture-of-experts architectures

#RadixArk #DaisyRose #ReinforcementLearning #AIAgents #OpenSource #LLM

Source: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency

item.title: RadixQuantVLA Unifies Vision‑Language‑Action Quantization
item.description:
RadixQuantVLA Unifies Vision‑Language‑Action Quantization

RadixQuantVLA, an active‑development framework, unifies post‑training quantization, benchmarking, and deployment preparation for Vision‑Language‑Action (VLA) models.

🔍 Overview

  • Unified, Lego‑like framework for VLA quantization, benchmarking, and deployment preparation.
  • Integrates routes: QuantVLA, Omega‑QVLA, QVLA/OpenVLA, FoldQuantVLA, OpenVLA‑OFT, OpenDriveLab/UniVLA, StarVLA, GR00T‑N1.5, and Pi0.5/OpenPI‑style.
  • Provides standardized launchers, checkpoint conventions, output formats, and validation on LIBERO benchmarks.

🧩 How it Works

RadixQuantVLA follows a modular, pipeline‑oriented view. Each route is a composable block that includes a model loader, quantization method, calibration context, benchmark suite, output artifact, and validation record. Calibration data, sensitivity analysis, layer protection, and route‑specific artifacts are treated as first‑class engineering objects.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Large checkpoints, quantized packs, datasets, and benchmark outputs are intentionally kept outside git.
  • Calibration context matches the model structure, rollout distribution, and task objective.
  • Standardized route names, launcher behavior, logs, summaries, and route‑level documentation.
  • Repaired OpenVLA‑OFT QVLA W8A16 route revalidated on LIBERO Spatial: BF16 99.0 % and mixed‑bit W8A16 98.0 % under a 100‑episode, seed‑7 protocol.

🚀 Availability

  • RadixQuantVLA is under active development.
  • Large assets are stored outside the Git repository.

💡 Why It Matters

  • A VLA policy couples visual perception, language‑conditioned reasoning, robot state, and action generation; its output is an executable robot action.
  • A small low‑bit error can propagate through perception, semantic grounding, action decoding, trajectory generation, contact dynamics, and closed‑loop control, making VLA quantization a behavior‑preserving compression problem.
  • Model size, token accuracy, or reconstruction error alone cannot determine whether a quantized policy still works; practical quantization must preserve action fidelity, temporal stability, semantic‑action alignment, and downstream task success.
  • Existing VLA quantization projects are fragmented; RadixQuantVLA consolidates these efforts into Lego‑like, named routes for inspection, comparison, reproduction, and extension.

#VLA #Quantization #RobotControl #OpenSource #VisionLanguage

Source: RadixRootMind/RadixQuantVLA

item.title: RTranslator: Offline Real-Time Translation App for Android
item.description:
RTranslator: Offline Real-Time Translation App for Android

RTranslator is an (almost) open-source, free, and offline real-time translation app for Android. It allows users to have conversations in real-time, even if they speak different languages.

🔍 Overview

  • RTranslator is a free, offline real-time translation app for Android.
  • It uses Meta’s NLLB for translation and OpenAi’s Whisper for speech recognition.
  • The app works even in the background, with the phone on standby or when using other apps.

🧩 How it works

  • The app has two main features: Conversation mode and WalkieTalkie mode.
  • In Conversation mode, you can connect with another phone that uses the app.
  • When you talk, your phone (or the Bluetooth headset, if connected) will capture the audio.
  • The audio captured will be converted into text and sent to the interlocutor’s phone.
  • The interlocutor’s phone will translate the text received into his language.
  • The interlocutor’s phone will convert the translated text into audio and will reproduce it from its speaker (or by the Bluetooth headset of the interlocutor if connected).
  • In WalkieTalkie mode, the smartphone microphone will listen in two languages simultaneously.
  • The app will detect in which language the interlocutor is speaking, translate the audio into the other language, convert the text into audio, and then reproduce it from the phone speaker.

⚙️ Key details

  • Each user can have more than one connected phone so that you can translate conversations between more than two people and in any combination.
  • The app only translates conversations between two people, it doesn’t work with Bluetooth headsets, and you have to talk in turns.
  • It’s not a real simultaneous translation, but it can work with only one phone.
  • RTranslator uses Meta’s NLLB for translation and OpenAi’s Whisper for speech recognition, both are (almost) open-source and state of the art AIs, have excellent quality and run directly on the phone, ensuring absolute privacy and the possibility of using RTranslator even offline without loss of quality.
  • The 3.0 version of RTranslator is currently funded through the [NGI Mobifree Fund], a fund established by [NLnet].
  • The NLLB translation model has been replaced with the option to choose between: Mozilla Bergamot models, Madlad 400 3B, and HY-MT 1.5 1.8B.
  • All these models have better translation quality than NLLB 54B, similar to Google Translate, with HY-MT 1.5 1.8B having much better scores than Google Translate, similar to DeepSeek v3 and Gemini 3.0.
  • MLKit has been replaced with open-source alternatives (FastText and Lingua), making RTranslator 100% open-source.

🚀 Availability

  • To install the app, download the latest version of the app apk file from https://github.com/niedev/RTranslator/releases/ and install it.
  • On the first launch, RTranslator will automatically download the models for translation and speech recognition (1.2GB) and once done you can start translating.
  • The initial download will get the models from GitHub, however in some regions GitHub is very slow, those who have problems of this kind can download the models separately from a computer (or in general in whatever way they prefer) and insert them manually into the app following this guide.

💡 Why it matters

  • RTranslator offers a unique solution for real-time translation, ensuring absolute privacy and the possibility of using the app even offline.
  • The app’s use of state-of-the-art AI models for translation and speech recognition ensures excellent quality.
  • RTranslator is funded through the [NGI Mobifree Fund], a fund established by [NLnet], which shows the potential and impact of the app.
  • The app’s 100% open-source nature, with the replacement of MLKit with open-source alternatives, makes it a significant step forward in the field of real-time translation apps.

#RTranslator #RealTimeTranslation #AndroidApp #OpenSource #OfflineTranslation

Source: niedev/RTranslator

item.description:
Curated Catalog of Open-Source MLSecOps Tools for AI Security

A new curated catalog has been released to help security engineers, machine learning practitioners, developers, and AI red teams discover resources for integrating security into the machine learning lifecycle.

🔍 Overview

MLSecOps (Machine Learning Security Operations) is the practice of integrating security throughout the machine learning lifecycle, spanning data collection, model development, deployment, monitoring, and incident response. This catalog compiles open-source tools, adversarial machine learning research, AI security frameworks, threat-modeling resources, and practical learning materials to support these efforts.

🧩 How it works

The catalog applies security testing, threat modeling, supply-chain protection, access controls, and continuous monitoring to machine learning models, MLOps pipelines, LLM applications, and AI agents. The resources are organized into specific functional categories:

Category Function
Model and artifact security tools Detect unsafe serialization, malicious payloads, integrity failures, and other risks in machine learning model files.
Adversarial machine learning testing tools Evaluate model robustness against evasion, poisoning, extraction, inversion, and other adversarial techniques.
Embodied AI and robotics ML security tools Test policies that emit actions rather than text, where a successful attack moves a robot out of its safe envelope rather than changing a prediction.

💡 Why it matters

Open-source MLSecOps tools allow practitioners to test, monitor, and protect machine learning models, data, pipelines, LLM applications, and AI agents. The catalog serves as a central discovery point for these resources, including active projects and proofs of concept.

item.title: FinRL-X launches as next-generation modular trading framework
item.description:
FinRL-X launches as next-generation modular trading framework

The AI4Finance Foundation has released FinRL-X, a next-generation evolution of the original FinRL framework. While the original repository remains available for education and research prototyping, the new release focuses on AI-native, modular, and production-oriented quantitative trading.

🧩 Evolution from Monolith to Modular

FinRL was recognized as the first open-source framework for financial reinforcement learning. It utilized a three-layer coupled monolith architecture with a train-test-trade pipeline.

FinRL-X transitions this paradigm from traditional Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) to an AI-Native approach that is ML + DRL + LLM-ready. The new architecture is fully decoupled into modular layers, designed for deployment-aware quantitative trading.

⚙️ Key Technical Differences

The transition to FinRL-X involves specific structural and functional changes across several key components:

Component Original FinRL FinRL-X
Paradigm Deep Reinforcement Learning AI-Native (ML + DRL + LLM-ready)
Architecture Three-layer coupled monolith Fully decoupled modular layers
Strategies DRL agents (A2C, DDPG, PPO, SAC, TD3) ML selection + DRL timing + extensible base
Data Layer 14 manually-wired processors Auto-select: Yahoo Finance → FMP → WRDS
Backtesting Custom hand-rolled evaluation loops Professional bt library engine
Live Trading Basic Alpaca support Full multi-account integration + risk controls
Configuration config.py + config_tickers.py Type-safe Pydantic + .env multi-env
Risk Management Gym environment constraints only Order, portfolio, and strategy-level controls

The framework is backed by research papers available on arXiv, including arXiv:2011.09607 and arXiv:2603.21330.

🚀 Component Availability

The ecosystem now includes FinRL-Meta for Gym-style financial market environments and benchmarks, alongside ElegantRL for lightweight and elegant DRL algorithms. The original FinRL repository preserves the end-to-end educational and research framework. For the latest architecture, live trading deployment, and production-focused development, users are directed to the FinRL-X / FinRL-Trading repository.

#FinRL #ReinforcementLearning #QuantTrading #OpenSource #AI

item.title: LLaVA-OneVision-2.5-4B-Instruct Released with Unified Video and Streaming Support
item.description:
LLaVA-OneVision-2.5-4B-Instruct Released with Unified Video and Streaming Support

🔍 Overview

On November 18, 2026, LLaVA-OneVision-2.5-4B-Instruct was released as the latest entry in the LLaVA-OneVision family. This release is a 4B model designed for single-image, multi-image, and video input that is also trained for streaming video. The release includes the training code alongside the model weights.

🧩 How it works

The model architecture supports two distinct video processing modes:

  • Long video: Enables multi-frame reasoning with efficient codec-aligned inference.
  • Streaming video: Frames arrive one at a time, and the model decides at every step whether to stay silent or speak.

The same weights and the same chat template serve both offline and streaming modes. Additionally, the model supports 3D-aware spatial reasoning, including depth, layout, and object relations. The design operates at native resolution without task-specific adapters.

⚙️ Key details

  • Model Size: 4B parameters.
  • Input Modalities: Single-image, multi-image, video, and 3D spatial data.
  • Training Efficiency: A tool named ResearchBoost-Agent made LLaVA-OneVision-2-4B SFT 2.2–3.0× faster.
  • Context: The underlying OneVision-Encoder uses HEVC-style vision transformers that add a codec-stream input mode. This approach selects motion- and residual-rich patches, allowing for dramatically longer temporal coverage under the same token budget compared to prior ViT backbones.

📦 Datasets

Four datasets ship with the LLaVA-OneVision family, including two new ones for LLaVA-OneVision-2 and two carried forward from 1.5:

Dataset Name Description
LLaVA-OneVision-2-VideoCaption Extremely dense video captions
LLaVA-OneVision-2-Spatial 3D-aware spatial reasoning
LLaVA-OneVision-1.5-Mid-Training-85M 85M concept-balanced mid-training corpus
LLaVA-OneVision-1.5-Instruct Full instruction-tuning mixture

💡 Why it matters

The LLaVA-OneVision-2 release was noted as a next-generation multimodal model with a fully open pipeline where encoder weights, training code, configs, and full training logs are released end-to-end. This commitment to transparency allows for detailed analysis of the training processes and architectural choices, such as the integration of codec-aligned vision encoders.

#LLaVA-OneVision #MultimodalAI #VideoUnderstanding #OpenSource #SpatialReasoning

item.title: Model Context Protocol Registry API Enters v0.1 API Freeze
item.description:
Model Context Protocol Registry API Enters v0.1 API Freeze

The community-driven Model Context Protocol (MCP) registry service has launched in preview and its Registry API (v0.1) has entered an API freeze.

🔍 Overview

  • The MCP registry provides MCP clients with a list of MCP servers, functioning like an app store for MCP servers.
  • The registry has launched in preview with an announcement blog post.
  • While the system is now more stable, this is still a preview release and breaking changes or data resets may occur.
  • A general availability (GA) release will follow later.

⚙️ Key details

  • For the next month or more, the API will remain stable with no breaking changes, allowing integrators to confidently implement support.
  • This freeze applies to v0.1 while development continues on v0.
  • This period will be used to validate the API in real-world integrations and gather feedback to shape v1 for general availability.
  • Publishing an MCP server does not happen through a pull request to the repository; adding a server.json, a server directory, or an entry in data/seed.json will not publish or list your server, even if the PR is merged.
  • Users must use the mcp-publisher CLI from their server’s own project instead.

🚀 Availability

  • The registry uses ko to build container images, and pre-built Docker images are automatically published to GitHub Container Registry.
  • Starting the registry at localhost:8080 with PostgreSQL uses ephemeral storage that resets each time containers are restarted.
  • By default, the registry seeds from the production API with a filtered subset of servers to keep startup fast.
  • The image does not bundle PostgreSQL, so users must run their own and point the registry at it via MCP_REGISTRY_DATABASE_URL.
  • Setup can be configured with environment variables in docker-compose.yml, and .env.example provides a reference.
  • Docker run commands are available for ghcr.io/modelcontextprotocol/registry:latest, :main, :v1.0.0, and :main-20250906-abc123d.

  • Radoslav (Rado) Dimitrov (Stacklok) [@rdimitrov] - WG Lead

item.title: RealmForge: Open-Source Platform for Persistent Swarms of LLM Agents
item.description:
RealmForge: Open-Source Platform for Persistent Swarms of LLM Agents

RealmForge is an open‑source platform that orchestrates large swarms of LLM‑powered agents within a persistent, graph‑based world.

🔍 Overview

  • Open‑source platform for orchestrating vast swarms of LLM‑powered agents, each with unique identities, goals, and evolving relationships.
  • Operates within a Structured World Model that persists across sessions.
  • Moves beyond simple chat‑based interactions to emergent narratives, economies, and simulated societies.

🧩 Architecture

  • World Conductor service manages temporal flow, advancing the simulation in tick‑based cycles.
  • Chronicler module records all events into a searchable lore database.
  • Structured World Model (SWM) is a directed graph of entities (agents, locations, objects, concepts) with properties, inventory, and narrative history.
  • Relationship Graph decays over time if not reinforced, mimicking fading memory.
  • Narrative Market where agent desires act as bids for attention; the World Conductor selects the most pressing conflict or opportunity and creates a Plot Thread.
  • Environmental Events (e.g., storm, festival, dragon sighting) are generated based on internal clocks or random rolls.

⚙️ Agent Design

  • Each agent has a Persona Script (core traits, goals, knowledge cut‑off) and a State Vector (mood, health, inventory, relationships).
  • Agents possess a Perception Radius, limiting visibility and interaction to nearby entities in the graph, creating realistic information asymmetry.
  • Agents can delegate tasks to sub‑agents, enabling recursive complexity.
  • Language‑agnostic persona system; entities store language tags, allowing multilingual interaction through diplomat agents or translation artifacts.

📈 Persistence & Emergence

  • The world is a queryable knowledge graph, not a flat text string.
  • Time advances in discrete Epochs (configurable from seconds to months of in‑world time); agents act based on schedules, task durations, and information propagation.
  • The simulation tracks resource scarcity, faction reputation, and character development over simulated days or years.

📋 Core Components

Component Role
Structured World Model Directed graph storing entities, properties, inventory, and narrative history
World Conductor Advances simulation ticks, selects Plot Threads from Narrative Market
Chronicler Records all events into a searchable lore database
Relationship Graph Tracks relationships; decays over time without reinforcement
Narrative Market Hosts agent desires as bids for attention
Environmental Event Engine Generates storms, festivals, dragon sightings, etc.

#AI #OpenSource #AgentSimulation #KnowledgeGraph

Source: Abhinesh2004/mirage-cortex

item.title: Reson8 Open Sources Rumble-2-Flash: A 0.5B Speech Recognition Model
item.description:
Reson8 Open Sources Rumble-2-Flash: A 0.5B Speech Recognition Model

Reson8 has open-sourced Rumble-2-Flash, a 0.5B-parameter speech recognition model, under the Apache 2.0 license. Designed for 40+ languages, the model competes with systems 3-60x its size while offering native support in Hugging Face Transformers and vLLM without requiring custom code.

🧩 How it works

Rumble-2-Flash utilizes the Qwen3-ASR architecture to ensure day-0 support. To determine how small a model could become before accuracy degraded, the team distilled Rumble-2, a larger production model, into this smaller version using on-policy distillation.

In this process, the student model does not train on transcripts written by the teacher. Instead, it transcribes the audio itself, and the teacher grades that transcript token by token. At every position, the teacher provides its own probability for the next token, and the student learns to match it. Because the student learns from its own outputs, it receives corrections for the specific mistakes it makes, with feedback on every token rather than a single score per clip.

On-policy distillation typically requires the teacher and student to share a tokenizer, which was not the case here. Choosing Qwen3-ASR meant adopting its vocabulary, so the team introduced GOLD to remove this restriction. GOLD merges tokens where the two tokenizers split text differently, allowing both models to be compared over the same text. Tokens present in both vocabularies are compared directly, while others are compared via their sorted probabilities.

⚙️ Key details

  • Languages: Supports 40+ languages with automatic language detection.
  • Output Control: Allows numbers as digits or words, management of fillers, verbatim repeats, and forced language settings.
  • Performance: Processes an hour of audio in about half a second, achieving over 7,000 RTFx on full batches.
  • Benchmarking: On the Open ASR Leaderboard multilingual track (Chinese, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, Dutch, and English), it averages a 6.96% error rate.
  • Comparison: This performance is better than Meta’s omniASR-LLM 7B (15x larger) and ahead of Whisper large-v3.
  • English Track: Averages a 6.6% WER.

On AppTek’s call-centre benchmark, which includes 302 hours of helpline calls and 14 English accents, Rumble-2-Flash reaches 7.86% WER. This result is on par with NVIDIA’s Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe (30B) at 7.78% and well ahead of Qwen3-ASR 0.6B (8.7%). It is close to Qwen3-ASR 1.7B (7.4%), the only model in the comparison that performs better.

item.title: SMART SDK and AgentCore Simplify WhatsApp Agent Deployment on AWS
item.description:
SMART SDK and AgentCore Simplify WhatsApp Agent Deployment on AWS

Across Latin America, India, and Southeast Asia, WhatsApp is one of the most widely used messaging applications, but building a robust agent on top of it requires handling complex, type-dependent payloads, media processing pipelines, and strict compliance rules. To simplify this process, SMART (Social Messaging Agent Runtime Toolkit) is available as an open source Python SDK and Terraform stack that provides the full channel layer for agents running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

🧩 How it works

SMART allows you to provide an agent that runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, and it handles the underlying channel logic. The architecture utilizes the following services:

  • AWS End User Messaging Social: Receives inbound WhatsApp messages and routes them to the processing layer.
  • AWS Lambda: Handles the channel logic, including verifying SNS message signatures, normalizing payloads, and rate-limiting users (20 messages per minute by default).
  • Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Provides the runtime, memory, and observability for the agent.
  • Supporting Services: Amazon DynamoDB (optional, for per-user state), AWS Secrets Manager, Amazon CloudWatch, and Amazon S3 supply state management, credentials, monitoring, and storage.

The AgentCore runtime hosts and scales the agent without requiring infrastructure management. AgentCore memory persists conversation history across sessions and deployments, scoped automatically to each phone number. The create_session_manager() function binds the agent to this memory, with a default retention period of 7 days. Frameworks such as Strands Agents get memory wired automatically, while LangGraph and Pydantic-AI can integrate with the conversation loop.

⚙️ Key details

Wiring up a custom WhatsApp agent typically involves configuring more than 10 AWS services and learning specific system behaviors. SMART abstracts these complexities, including:

  • Inbound message authentication and normalization.
  • Processing pipelines for media such as voice notes, images, and documents.
  • Durable schedules for reminders and authenticated paths for external systems to trigger outbound messages.
  • Compliance with Meta’s requirement that messages sent more than 24 hours after the user’s last message must use pre-approved templates.
  • Handling of intermediate tool outputs (like button lists or progress updates) to prevent conversation history corruption.

🚀 Availability

SMART is an open source solution. A single command deploys the entire infrastructure to your AWS account. Webmotors, originally scoped as a two-month engagement, compressed delivery to six weeks and moved their internal team into controlled production ahead of a full launch using this approach.

#WhatsApp #AmazonBedrock #AIAgents #AWS #OpenSource

Source: Build WhatsApp AI agents with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services

item.title: AI Coding Agent Optimized with TokenEconomizer
item.description:
AI Coding Agent Optimized with TokenEconomizer

TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that reduces waste in AI coding agent sessions by learning from past sessions and adapting to future ones.

🔍 Overview

TokenEconomizer is a plugin that learns from an agent’s past sessions in a repository to reduce waste in future sessions, without modifying the agent or its underlying model.

🧩 How it works

  • The agent sends instructions, tool descriptions, and session history to its model.
  • TokenEconomizer reads the session’s log and updates what it knows about the repository.
  • Micro-skills capture repository-specific knowledge in one-line notes.
  • Tool pruning removes tools that repository history suggests the agent is unlikely to use, while always retaining core tools for running commands and editing files.
  • Failure-loop intervention watches for an agent that keeps hitting the same failure.

⚙️ Key details

  • TokenEconomizer reduced costs by 18.4–30.9% across multiple AI coding agents on 277 real bug-fixing tasks.
  • Costs fell in every repository tested, while task success rates remained broadly stable.
  • The agent received 23 tool descriptions on every turn, but 16 were never called.

🚀 Availability

TokenEconomizer is available as an open-source plugin from UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Microsoft Security.

💡 Why it matters

TokenEconomizer reduces waste without changing the agent or its underlying model, so developers can use it alongside the coding agents they already rely on.

📊 Evaluation

  • TokenEconomizer lowered the average cost by 18.4–30.9% on 277 SWE-Bench tasks from six repositories, using five different AI coding agent and model combinations.
  • The savings also carried over to sequential web development, with costs 16.0–21.2% lower on Web-Bench.
  • On security auditing, where every task is in a new repository, costs were 6.4–19.6% lower.

📸 Images

  • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/TokenEconomizer-BlogHeroFeature-1400x788-1.jpg

#AIagents #Open-source #Plugin #Optimization

item.title: Apple Machine Learning Research Releases MLX Array Framework for Apple Silicon
item.description:
Apple Machine Learning Research Releases MLX Array Framework for Apple Silicon

Apple machine learning research has introduced MLX, an array framework designed for machine learning on Apple silicon. The framework is designed by machine learning researchers for machine learning researchers, with the goal of being user-friendly while remaining efficient to train and deploy models.

🔍 Overview

MLX provides multiple APIs designed to mirror existing popular frameworks:

  • NumPy-like Python API: A Python API that closely follows NumPy.
  • Multi-Language Support: Fully featured C++, C, and Swift APIs that closely mirror the Python API.
  • PyTorch-like Higher-level Packages: Packages like mlx.nn and mlx.optimizers with APIs that closely follow PyTorch to simplify building more complex models.

🧩 How it works

MLX features several architectural choices that optimize usability and performance:

  • Lazy Computations: Computations in MLX are lazy, meaning arrays are only materialized when needed.
  • Dynamic Graph Construction: Computation graphs are constructed dynamically. This ensures that changing the shapes of function arguments does not trigger slow compilations, making debugging simple and intuitive.
  • Shared Memory: Arrays in MLX live in shared memory, enabling operations on arrays to run on any supported device type without transferring data.
  • Multi-Device Support: Operations can run on any supported device, currently including the CPU and the GPU.
  • Composable Transformations: MLX supports composable function transformations for automatic differentiation, automatic vectorization, and computation graph optimization.

⚙️ Key details

The MLX software suite was initially developed with equal contribution by Awni Hannun, Jagrit Digani, Angelos Katharopoulos, and Ronan Collobert.

MLX is available on PyPI. Additionally, users can install a CPU-only Linux package or the CUDA backend on Linux. The MLX examples repository also offers a variety of examples.

#MLX #AppleSilicon #MachineLearning #OpenSource

Source: ml-explore/mlx

item.title: Ax Ships a TypeScript-First, Multi-Language LLM Toolkit
item.description:
Ax Ships a TypeScript-First, Multi-Language LLM Toolkit

Ax is a TypeScript-first development toolkit that ships as @ax-llm/ax. Its shared semantic core is also compiled into generated Python, Java, C++, Go, and Rust libraries.

🔍 Overview

Ax provides typed structured generation, deployment profiles, agents, flows, and optimizers. The TypeScript package is the source implementation and current published package.

🧩 How it works

Signatures for typed structured generation can be written using:

  • A string DSL
  • The fluent f() builder
  • Any Standard Schema v1 validator, including Zod, Valibot, and ArkType

The deployment name selects wire behavior, while the model ID is resolved inside that deployment. Named deployment profiles cover native APIs, routers, hosted inference, configurable runtimes, audio, and realtime event streams.

For example:

1
2
3

const llm = ai({ name: "openai", apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_APIKEY });
const classify = ax('review:string -> sentiment:class "positive, negative, neutral"',);
await classify.forward(llm, { review: "This product is amazing!" })

The evidence describes this example as requiring no prompt engineering. The provider name can be switched from "openai" to "anthropic", "google-gemini", "meta", "together", "fireworks", "deepseek", or "grok", among others.

⚙️ Key details

  • Agents: runtime execution, context budgets, checkpoints, action-log replay, discovery, memory, skills, and delegation.
  • Flows: typed program graphs supporting branches, loops, feedback, cache behavior, parallel execution, and .returns(...) projection.
  • Optimizers: GEPA, few-shot bootstrapping, portable optimizer artifacts, and evaluation/apply flows.
  • Runtime path: Ax is designed to stay in the same latency class as direct provider calls while adding typed outputs, validation, retries, tools, tracing, and memory. Its hot path renders the signature, calls the provider, parses the result, and returns a typed value.
  • Streaming: Streaming is the default. Ax can parse fields as they arrive, run streaming assertions, fail early, cancel an in-flight stream, and start correction.

🚀 Availability

Language Package or distribution Availability
TypeScript / JavaScript @ax-llm/ax Published on npm
Python axllm Published on PyPI
Java dev.axllm:ax Published on Maven Central
C++ axllm::axllm CMake FetchContent source build
Go github.com/ax-llm/ax/packages/go Installable with go get
Rust axllm Published on crates.io

The same signatures, provider mappings, agents, flows, runtime contracts, and optimizers are compiled into verified generated Python, Java, C++, Go, and Rust libraries.

item.title: Chromatone Offers an Open-Source Digital Garden of Visual Music Theory
item.description:
Chromatone Offers an Open-Source Digital Garden of Visual Music Theory

Chromatone has been introduced as an independent open-source research project to use colors, shapes, and motion to learn, play, and communicate melody, harmony, and rhythms in live music performance environments. It functions as both a digital garden of visual music theory and a collection of visual music instruments.

🔍 Overview

Chromatone provides scientific research on many aspects of music theory as cards and short overviews focusing on the physics and physiology of vision and hearing, alongside their intersection in visual music research, exploration, practice, and self-expression. The project consists of progressive web-apps designed to be carried in a pocket for everyday music practice, including open-source web-experiments featuring interactive combinations of sounds and colors.

🧩 Key Features

  • Interactive Experiments: Open-source tools for sound analysis and synthesis, allowing users to experiment with various media instruments.
  • Modular Music Theory Data: Neatly stored lists of intervals, chords, scales, and rhythmic patterns from different cultures provided in YAML format.
  • Developer Integration: Everything is available as a treeshakeable NPM package that can be integrated into any JS project on both the server-side (SSR) and the client-side.
  • Educational Utility: The project abstracts low-level details into simple building blocks, making it a functional tool for prototyping and concept verification by audio researchers, educators, and students.

item.title: Community members step in to maintain Distilabel synthetic data framework
item.description:
Community members step in to maintain Distilabel synthetic data framework

The original authors of Distilabel, a framework for synthetic data and AI feedback, have moved on to other projects. In response, a group of community members has recently joined the GitHub project as collaborators to maintain it and are actively working towards the next release. In the meantime, users can check out the develop branch for access to the latest fixes and improvements.

🔍 Overview

Distilabel is an open-source, community-driven framework designed for engineers who need fast, reliable, and scalable pipelines based on verified research papers. Its goal is to accelerate AI development by quickly generating high-quality, diverse datasets for synthesizing and judging data using AI feedback. By focusing on data quality, Distilabel aims to tackle the root causes of expensive compute and output quality issues, allowing users to spend their time achieving high-quality standards.

🧩 How it works

Distilabel uses a programmatic approach to build scalable pipelines for data generation and AI feedback. It integrates AI feedback from any LLM provider using one unified API, ensuring flexibility, scalability, and fault tolerance while leveraging the latest research papers.

💡 Why it matters

The framework helps users synthesize and judge data for a wide variety of projects, including:

  • Traditional predictive NLP (classification, extraction).
  • Generative and large language model scenarios (instruction following, dialogue generation, judging).
  • Ownership of data for fine-tuning custom LLMs.

The Argilla community uses distilabel to create datasets and models, such as:

  • The 1M OpenHermesPreference, a dataset of ~1 million AI preferences derived from teknium/OpenHermes-2.5, demonstrating large-scale data synthesis.
  • The distilabeled Intel Orca DPO dataset and improved OpenHermes model, which show performance improvements by filtering out 50% of the original dataset through AI feedback.
  • The haiku DPO data, which outlines how anyone can create a specific task dataset using the latest research papers to improve quality.

⚙️ Key details

anthropic For using models available in Anthropic API via the AnthropicLLM integration.
cohere For using models available in Cohere via the CohereLLM integration.

item.title: Haiku RAG Launches Open-Source Agentic Retrieval System with Docling and Ollama
item.description:
Haiku RAG Launches Open-Source Agentic Retrieval System with Docling and Ollama

A new open-source project called Haiku RAG has been released, offering an agentic retrieval-augmented generation system that answers questions about user documents with citations to page numbers and section headings. The system runs on an embedded LanceDB database with open models through Ollama by default, requiring no server or API key. It supports multiple providers via Pydantic AI, and the same database can live on S3, GCS, Azure, or LanceDB Cloud. Built on LanceDB, Pydantic AI, and Docling, it ingests PDFs, office documents, HTML, Markdown, and images. The stored DoclingDocument preserves headings, tables, pictures, and page provenance. Search utilizes hybrid vector and full-text retrieval, optional reranking with cross-encoders and various providers, section-aware context expansion, and image search with multimodal embedders. It can answer with RAG capability, searching, running sandboxed Python for counting and aggregation, and citing page numbers and headings. Vision models receive figures directly. Optional capabilities compact earlier evidence and require answers to declare grounding. Citations can be checked by drawing chunks on page images from CLI, chat TUI, or Python. Integration options include Python API, native Pydantic AI capabilities, plugin hooks, MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, and Claude Desktop, plus a reference web app. The haiku-ingester service supports filesystem, HTTP, S3, and WebDAV sources with a SQLite or Postgres job queue, control plane, dashboard, tags, rollback, vacuum, and health checks. Python 3.12 or newer is required. Installation offers two packages: pip install haiku.rag for full features including Docling, VoyageAI, Cohere embedders, all rerankers, and TUI; and pip install haiku.rag-slim for core with extras. Default configuration uses Ollama for embeddings and answers. Commands include haiku-rag init, haiku-rag add-src, haiku-rag search, haiku-rag ask, haiku-rag chat, and haiku-rag mcp --stdio. The ingester service runs separately with haiku-ingester serve and supports continuous ingestion from configured sources.

#AI #RAG #OpenSource #LLM #Docling #LanceDB

Source: ggozad/haiku.rag

mlx-audio library brings TTS and STS models to Apple Silicon

Neywa Labs, the company behind Nativ, has released mlx-audio, an open-source library built on Apple’s MLX framework.   • Interface: An interactive web interface with 3D audio visualization.

item.title: NVIDIA launches Dynamo as open-source datacenter-scale inference orchestration layer
item.description:
NVIDIA launches Dynamo as open-source datacenter-scale inference orchestration layer

NVIDIA has announced Dynamo, an open-source, datacenter-scale inference stack built in Rust and Python that serves as an orchestration layer above existing inference engines. Dynamo does not replace SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or vLLM; instead, it turns them into a coordinated multi-node inference system.

🧩 How it works

Dynamo integrates several key capabilities to optimize performance across diverse workloads:

  • Disaggregated serving for efficient resource allocation
  • Intelligent routing to direct requests optimally
  • Multi-tier KV caching to reduce latency
  • Automatic scaling to adapt to workload demand

These features work together to maximize throughput and minimize latency for LLM, reasoning, multimodal, and video generation workloads.

⚙️ Key details

The platform is designed for extensibility and performance:

item.title: Pagekin: Open-source AI novel writing app
item.description:
Pagekin: Open-source AI novel writing app

Pagekin, formerly AI Novel Writer, is a free, open-source AI novel writing app designed for long novels and web fiction. It is local-first, with no model bundled, and available for Windows and macOS. Maintained by EthanYoQ, Pagekin allows users to write and manage their works locally on their own computers.

🔍 Overview

  • Free, open-source AI novel writing app
  • Designed for long novels and web fiction
  • Local-first, no model bundled
  • Available for Windows and macOS
  • Maintained by EthanYoQ

🧩 How it works

  • Works exist on your own computer
  • Software does not bundle models; users can connect their own API Key or use Ollama to run local models
  • Supports importing novels in .txt, .md, or .epub formats
  • Architecture page is divided into four sections: story premise, character list, world view, and plot outline
  • Each character has basic settings, current status, and relationship map
  • Character cards can be pasted or imported from files
  • Blueprint page lists planned chapters
  • Batch creation allows writing up to 10 chapters at a time
  • AI uses the chapter’s blueprint, relevant characters, world view, summary of previous text, and the full text of the previous chapter
  • Text editor supports inserting two full-width spaces as paragraph indentation
  • All generation tasks are managed in the running side page, divided into ongoing, history, and diagnostic pages
  • Tracks main plot, subplots, and foreshadowing by chapter
  • Knowledge base can be imported with reference materials in .txt or .md formats
  • Export options include merged Markdown, chaptered Markdown, or TXT
  • Works can be saved locally or backed up to a WebDAV cloud service
  • Writing skills can be selected from a local folder or single SKILL.md file, or from a GitHub address
  • Available in light and dark themes
  • Supports Chinese and English interfaces
  • Supports OpenAI compatible and Gemini native protocols
  • Built-in presets for various service providers: DeepSeek, SiliconFlow, BigModel, OpenAI, xAI, Google Gemini, Ollama, NovelAI, and custom
  • Semantic search in the knowledge base requires a separate vector model, configurable in the retrieval model settings
  • Upgrades only update the application itself, preserving works, character cards, and settings
  • Supports arm64 for Apple Silicon Macs (M1, M2, M3, M4, etc.)

🚀 Availability

  • Free, open-source
  • Windows & macOS
  • Supports arm64 for Apple Silicon Macs

💡 Why it matters

  • Provides a local-first approach to AI novel writing
  • Offers flexibility in model usage and integration
  • Supports multiple export and backup options
  • Allows for detailed character and plot management
  • Supports multiple languages and themes
  • Offers a range of service provider presets
  • Ensures data privacy by keeping works and settings local
  • Preserves user data during upgrades

#AIWriting #OpenSource #NovelWriting #AITools #WebFiction

item.title: Rust-Powered Multi-Protocol Download Manager Features Dynamic Acceleration and AI Agent Integration
item.description:
Rust-Powered Multi-Protocol Download Manager Features Dynamic Acceleration and AI Agent Integration

A new open-source download manager powered by Rust and the Tokio engine has been released as a free alternative to IDM. The tool features dynamic download acceleration with adaptive segmentation and is designed to be AI-agent ready through a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

🔍 Overview

The manager is a local-first, multi-protocol solution that requires no account for local downloads and contains zero advertisements. It uses a shared Rust + Tokio engine that remains independent of the UI and Foreign Function Interface (FFI), allowing it to power various client types from a single core.

  • Multi-protocol support: Handles HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, BitTorrent (including magnet links), eD2K, and streaming via HLS and DASH.
  • Cross-platform clients: Native GPUI desktop apps, Kotlin Android and SwiftUI iOS apps, a React Web UI, and a standalone CLI.
  • Browser integration: Includes a 3-layer interception engine for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox, supplemented by a userscript.

🧩 How it works

The engine implements dynamic download acceleration by splitting segments at runtime. If a segment is performing poorly, idle workers utilize a “slow-segment rescue” feature to take over the task. For persistence, the manager uses SQLite with Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) by default to store resumable states, while server deployments have the option to use PostgreSQL.

Protocol Capabilities
BitTorrent Supports DHT, UPnP, and magnet links
eD2K / eMule Server and Kad DHT source finding with MD4 verification
HLS / DASH Streaming media sniffing and AES-decryption support
Automation RSS subscriptions, scheduled queues, and JavaScript plugins

⚙️ Key details

The software includes professional-grade management tools such as named queues, global token-bucket rate limiting, and connection diagnostics. For developers and power users, it provides several integration paths:

  • AI Readiness: A built-in MCP server with 12 tools allows Claude, Cursor, and other AI clients to manage downloads.
  • Remote Management: Optional FluxCloud device collaboration for settings sync, remote task management, and LAN device pairing.
  • API Support: Offers REST/OpenAPI and aria2-compatible JSON-RPC interfaces.
  • Privacy: Anonymous installation and daily-active statistics can be disabled via settings and do not collect task-specific information.

🚀 Availability

The manager is available across multiple platforms including Windows, macOS, Linux, NAS, and Android. The desktop version includes a system tray service to keep downloads active after the main UI is closed. Users can choose between native GPUI interfaces or a React-based web management console, both supporting light, dark, and custom themes.

#Rust #OpenSource #AIagents #MCP #DownloadManager

Source: zerx-lab/FluxDown

item.title: Sovereign Core Unveils Open-Source AI-Driven Simulation Engine
item.description:
Sovereign Core Unveils Open-Source AI-Driven Simulation Engine

This week, Sovereign Core announced a new open‑source simulation platform that integrates a robust AI orchestration layer, a fault‑tolerant state grid, and a responsive command interface.

🔍 Overview

  • Provides a complete backend runtime, AI orchestration layer, and a responsive command interface for sovereign simulation environments.
  • Suitable for supply‑chain resilience, crisis response protocol testing, and synthetic training grounds for autonomous agents.
  • Delivers the structural integrity of a military‑grade simulation while remaining an open‑source framework.

🧩 How It Works

  • Fault‑tolerant grid distributes state, enabling operators to zoom from a macro‑level theater of operations down to individual asset behaviors without latency penalties.
  • Temporal event bus decouples simulation speed from rendering speed, allowing real‑time navigation of past, present, and speculative future states as layers.
  • The command interface is built on a reactive component architecture that consumes these layers without blocking input, ensuring fluid interaction even with tens of thousands of active entities.
  • A custom gleam‑engine propagates state updates in sub‑millisecond time across all connected clients.
  • A built‑in translation and localization pipeline supports English, Japanese, German, and Arabic, including a community‑driven framework for additional locales.
  • Natural‑language commands (voice or text) are parsed and executed in real time.
  • The UI adapts not only to screen size but also to operator role: logistics officers and tactical directors interact with different but synchronized control sets.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Cortical adapter treats the simulation as a sensorium for intelligent agents; the same APIs can be used by both human and AI operators.
  • The adapter allows pluggable backends—from lightweight heuristics to large language models running on private infrastructure.
  • An event‑sourced, lock‑free concurrency model underpins the simulation, making it a deterministic state machine that can be checkpointed, rewound, or forked.
  • Features speculative “what‑if” branches, scenario replay, and distributed computation across clusters.
  • The engine is written in a memory‑safe language with zero‑cost abstractions, enabling it to run on anything from a developer laptop to a dedicated server farm.
  • A built‑in health circuit monitors subsystems; upon failure (network partition, node crash, or data corruption), it automatically re‑routes and re‑establishes state, with structured, encrypted logs available for post‑mortem analysis.

🚀 Availability

  • The initial deployment package contains:
    • Core simulation runtime
    • Sample neural command agent
    • Bilingual (English / Japanese) interface template

💡 Why It Matters

  • The platform’s architecture allows for latency‑free, multi‑scale simulation, essential for realistic training and operational planning.
  • By integrating AI through a cortical adapter, future systems can expand to autonomous decision‑making within the same simulation environment.

#open-source #simulation #ai #distributed-systems #cognitive-computing

Source: endend2003-cmd/Tactical-Matrix-Console

item.title: Verlihub Advanced NMDC Protocol Server Supports More Than 25k Users
item.description:
Verlihub Advanced NMDC Protocol Server Supports More Than 25k Users

Verlihub is an advanced NMDC+S protocol server for Linux and Windows operating systems. It offers a high-performance solution with low RAM and CPU usage, capable of holding more than 25,000 users.

🔍 Overview

Verlihub provides high-level functionality for managing connections, hub administration, and security features. It uses epoll on Linux and Windows, and supports worker threads for slow work to maintain performance efficiency.

⚙️ Key details

  • Resource Efficiency: Low RAM and CPU usage using epoll on both Linux and Windows operating systems.
  • Capacity: Able to hold more than 25,000 users.
  • Security: Built-in TLS-encrypted connections using OpenSSL, supporting plain and encrypted users on the same port. An external TLS proxy is also supported, sending the real address of the user with the $MyIP command.
  • Database Support: Offers backup and restore functionality for MySQL or MariaDB databases.
  • Customization and Localization: Allows extending functionality via Lua scripts (including HTTP requests) and supports hub messages in many languages.
  • User and Connection Management: Handles user management with privileges, clients and connections management, and logging of user IPs and complete MyINFOs (requires Ledokol).
  • GeoIP Integration: Tracks the GeoIP country, city, and ASN of users using MaxMindDB.
  • Statistics: Generates statistics for your hub (requires Ledokol).

🚀 Availability

Verlihub builds on Windows with MinGW-w64, with dependencies and build steps detailed in Install.md. TLS support is built-in using OpenSSL and enabled by default; to build without it, the -DUSE_TLS=OFF flag can be used.

Several resources are available for support and integration:

  • Website: https://github.com/verlihub
  • Wiki: https://github.com/verlihub/verlihub/wiki
  • Crash: https://crash.verlihub.net
  • Translate: https://explore.transifex.com/feardc/verlihub
  • Ledokol: https://ledo.feardc.net
  • MMDB: https://ledo.feardc.net/mmdb
  • Support: nmdcs://hub.verlihub.net:7777
